title: Barcelona seal €50m deal with PSG for Ferran Torres
description: The Shark is heading for the French capital.
fullText:
Barcelona have reached a final agreement with Paris Saint-Germain for Ferran Torres in a deal which will see the Spain star head to Parc des Princes on a transfer worth €50 million.

The two clubs have been in talks for a while and the deal is now done, according to Fabrizio Romano. Torres has been absent from Barcelona training for the last two days and is now heading to Paris to complete his move.

🚨🔴🔵 BREAKING: Ferran Torres to Paris Saint-Germain, HERE WE GO! 💥

Deal confirmed for World Cup final hero as Barça receive a fee worth €50m from PSG.

Ferran only wanted Paris and the agreement has been sealed after being at final stages for several days. All done. pic.twitter.com/4siCHz3yIc

Torres will sign a five-year contract with PSG and link up with Luis Enrique's side after scoring the winning goal for Spain in the World Cup final.

The 26-year-old was into the final year of his contract at Barcelona but will now seek a new challenge in Ligue 1 with the French giants.

Barcelona had reportedly been reluctant to extend Torres's contract, as they would have had to pay an extra €8 million to Manchester City, while there's been speculation the Spain star was happy to move on after feeling undervalued by Barca.

title: Be prepared for the preseason with our Atlanta Falcons roster
description: All of the Falcons players are sorted by their jersey numbers and by their last names to help you find your favorites during the preseason.
fullText:
The Falcons preseason is upon us, with Atlanta facing off against the Denver Broncos in Week 1, the Indianapolis Colts in Week 2, and the Miami Dolphins in Week 3. This will be a very different preseason than fans are accustomed to, as head coach Kevin Stefanski made it clear that starters will play—for about a series or so—in at least the first and third games. Both Arthur Smith and Raheem Morris were very reluctant to play any starters in preseason.

The team best known for playing starters in the preseason might be the Kansas City Chiefs, who often have their first string play up to an entire half in preparation for the season. That strategy seemed to work out well for the Chiefs, who are perennial contenders and will be right back in the mix this season with a healthy Patrick Mahomes. The Chiefs are tied for the fourth in the current Super Bowl odds at +1700, well above Atlanta's current position at +8000.

To that end, we've got a sorted roster here to help you keep track of your preseason darlings this summer. We've got this sorted two ways: by number, low to high; and by last name, A to Z. That can help you more quickly identify players, especially those who are new faces to the Falcons. I've also got my own printable version of the Falcons 2026 roster that you can find here.

We hope that this roster will aid you in your viewing of Atlanta's preseason. We'll try to keep it as updated as we can, so check back closer to game time for the most recent version!

title: Red Sox's Ceddanne Rafaela named AL MVP candidate by ESPN with Yordan Alvarez problem
description: Is Rafaela a top-25 player in Major League Baseball?
fullText:
Red Sox's Ceddanne Rafaela named AL MVP candidate by ESPN with Yordan Alvarez problem originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Center fielder Ceddane Rafaela has been one of the top players for the Boston Red Sox as they've returned to postseason contention.

Rafaela is one of the top defensive outfielders in baseball and has had a career year at the plate.

Recently, ESPN ranked him as the 27th-best player in the Majors for the 2026 season. Jorge Castillo went as far as to say that he should receive American League MVP consideration.

"As one of the premier defenders in baseball, the floor for Rafaela was always considered high. His offense, always streaky, would determine the ceiling. This season, the ceiling is MVP-caliber-high," Castillo wrote.

Rafaela has 16 defensive runs saved and 14 outs above average in center field. He earned his first All-Star selection thanks to a mix of power and speed that has produced 16 home runs and 16 stolen bases.

MORE: Dodgers prospect Kendall George to undergo knee surgery months after viral bat dog incident

"This isn't just another hot stretch for Rafaela. He has been raking for essentially half of a season. In 78 games since May 5, he's batting .295 with 15 home runs and an .827 OPS. He's 13-for-44 with four home runs in August," Castillo added. "He's an all-around dynamo. If he continues producing at the plate, a top-five MVP finish is very possible."

Even with a historic final few months, Rafaela will not surpass Yordan Alvarez, who could win the first Triple Crown since 2012, in the MVP race.

But as Castillo detailed, a top-five finish is in play for the 25-year-old from Curaçao.

title: LIV Golf finally stops selling tickets for doomed Michigan tournament
description: LIV Golf was set to host its team championship at The Cardinal at Saint John's Resort in Plymouth Township in late August.
fullText:
LIV Golf finally has stopped selling tickets for its team championship in Michigan.

It's the latest and most-definitive sign that the tournament set for The Cardinal at Saint John's Resort is not going to happen, amid the league's funding crisis. The tournament had been scheduled to be played Aug. 27-30.

LIV Golf hasn't yet made an official announcement about the event being canceled, though multiple reports over the last several months have pointed to that being the outcome. There has been no infrastructure buildout at The Cardinal, which drew tens of thousands of fans during LIV Golf's team championship in 2025. That was LIV Golf's first tournament held in Michigan.

LIV Golf still was selling tickets to the team championship in Michigan as of Wednesday night. On Thursday afternoon, on LIV Golf's website, ticket inquiries were met with the message: "The tickets you were looking for are no longer available." There was no further information, including details on refunds.

A report from The Telegraph this week said players finally have been officially informed that the team championship in Michigan was off, and last week, a TNT host on the LIV Golf broadcast from the tournament in New Jersey said that next week's tournament in Indianapolis would now determine the league's 2026 team champion.

Officials from The Cardinal have declined comment on the tournament's status, deferring to LIV Golf brass.

LIV Golf is in crisis mode after its chief financial backer, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, announced earlier this year that it was pulling out amid billions in losses since the league's debut in 2022. LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil announced last week that he had struck a deal with a new lead investor, though the investor wasn't identified and is believed to hinge on player commitments beyond 2026.

On that front, LIV Golf might've just been dealt a massive blow, with The Telegraph reporting Thursday that one of its star players, Jon Rahm, is "resigned" to leaving the league after 2026. He is believed to be owed $100 million-plus. Brooks Koepka left LIV Golf and returned to the PGA Tour this year, and Patrick Reed departed LIV Golf this year, too.

This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: LIV Golf finally stops selling tickets for doomed Michigan tournament

title: Jayden Daniels’ bizarre LSU beef is petty and sad at the same time
description: Jayden Daniels is acting like he’s bigger than the program at LSU. It’s a terrible look.
fullText:
Jayden Daniels' run to the Heisman Trophy with the LSU Tigers in 2023 was one of the most electric quarterback seasons in the recent history of college football. Daniels threw for 3,812 yards, 40 touchdowns, and only four interceptions in 12 games as LSU finished 10-3 with a win in the ReliaQuest Bowl.

Now Daniels is beefing with his former college program after they gave away his No. 5 to a player on this year's team. That's just the start of it.

Daniels' lawyers sent LSU a cease-and-desist saying it can no longer use his name, image and likeness, according to ESPN. Daniels' camp issued a statement saying his family is "deeply disappointed and feels profoundly disrespected" by the Tigers' decision to give No. 5 to sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett.

"The Daniels family is deeply disappointed and feels profoundly disrespected by LSU's decision to give Jayden's number to another player," the statement from Daniels' spokesperson said. "Jayden and his family had every reason to believe that his number would remain a meaningful part of his LSU legacy and would be honored and protected in recognition of his extraordinary contributions to the university."

At the crux of Daniels' frustration seems to be the way LSU treats Joe Burrow's legacy compared to his. No LSU player has worn Burrow's No. 9 since he left campus. Burrow won the 2019 Heisman Trophy and led the Tigers to the national championship. While Daniels bested Burrow's ridiculous numbers, his team finished only 10-3 and capped the year with a win in the ReliaQuest Bowl.

Neither Burrow or Daniels' number is retired by LSU, and school policy states that a player must have "completed competition for five years before being nominated for jersey retirement."

In another strange twist, LSU beat reporter Matt Moscona reported that Daniels requested LSU return its copy of his Heisman Trophy. Moscona noted that Daniels "personally reached out to LSU leadership" to express his displeasure, and that the school is still deciding how to handle it.

Here's the letter from Daniels' attorney:

The letter from Jayden Daniels’ attorney Adam Kenner to LSU football stating the program “must immediately cease and desist from any further use, display, publication, distribution, promotion, commercialization, or other exploitation of Mr. Daniels’ NIL in any manner or medium.” pic.twitter.com/QdX6Tl1evG

Former LSU star and former ESPN talking head Ryan Clark said that Daniels' camp understands that his number is not retired at LSU, and they haven't asked for it to be retired.

Pickett wore No. 3 at LSU as a freshman. New Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin said Pickett was promised No. 5 on the recruiting trail by former head coach Brian Kelly. Kelly stated that he didn't give Pickett No. 5 last season because Daniels was uncomfortable with it. On Pickett getting No. 5 this year, Kiffin said: "When a kid is promised something to come to a school, he should wear it. So at that point, I don't think that's really my decision. We should honor what he was told."

Pickett's father responded on Thursday in an interview with The Advocate, and said his son will not be changing his number. "This right here makes us want to wear the number more," he said. An assistant coach tweeted this photo with Pickett on Thursday:

#5 @LSUfootball #GeauxTigers #LSU pic.twitter.com/NQVs4z6Zd0

It's clear that Daniels feels like he's being disrespected compared to Burrow. He also doesn't have a legal leg to stand on here. This statement from Daniels' camp feels totally out of touch.

"Jayden made it clear that he did not want his number given to another player, and he believed his wishes would be respected," the statement said. "His Heisman Trophy-winning season and everything he accomplished on and off the field cemented his place in LSU history. To see his number given to another player is incredibly disappointing and feels like a failure to honor the significance of what Jayden accomplished at LSU."

Burrow helped lead LSU to its first national championship of the playoff era. Daniels' numbers might be slightly better on a spreadsheet, but it doesn't hit the same when his team lost to Florida State, Ole Miss, and Alabama during the season. It doesn't help that Daniels had something of a sophomore slump in the NFL last year with the Washington Commanders after a brilliant rookie season. Daniels looked like the best QB from the 2024 draft class after his first year, but going into this season, Drake Maye and Caleb Williams have surpassed him in rankings by most major publications.

Daniels needs to worry about creating his own NFL legacy, and stop holding onto his college days so closely. Anyone who watched Daniels at LSU knows how great he was. It's ridiculous to think he has ownership over a number for a college football program that has existed for more than 130 years when he was only on campus for two years. If he can have the same success with the Commanders, it's likely no one in Washington will ever wear his No. 5 again.

title: UConn women’s soccer 2026 season preview
description: Despite being in the midst of a rebuild, expectations are high for the Huskies.
fullText:
Expectations are high for UConn women's soccer entering the 2026 season. The Huskies were picked to finish second in the Big East and nabbed two first-place votes along the way. Meanwhile, women's college soccer guru Chris Henderson projected UConn as the top team in the conference, noting that "if you want to kill the league's giants, this is the year."

And yet, according to Rodriguez, her team is in the midst of a transition.

"We're in a little bit of a rebuild," she told The UConn Blog on Tuesday. "I've got a lot of new faces, whether they're freshmen, transfers, or even our returners filling new roles. So I'm confident with who we are and our foundation and our structure, but we gotta get these players up to speed quickly."

After an 11-4-3 season in 2025 in which they were left out of the NCAA Tournament despite ranking 44th in RPI, the Huskies lost nine players who started at least a game. With so many holes to plug, UConn turned to the transfer portal.

Historically, the Huskies have largely relied on homegrown talent while mixing in a few transfers. This year, they brought in a record six new players through the portal. Some replaced outgoing transfers, but the others were added specifically to bolster the roster.

"We weeded out some players that we felt maybe found better homes," Rodriguez said. "It was time to bring in a little bit more. We needed a little bit more experience to come in."

The head coach likes what she's seen so far through preseason practices and a pair of exhibitions. In a 0-0 draw with UMass, UConn showed off its strong defensive structure and created plenty of scoring chances, but struggled to finish. Against UNH on Sunday, the Huskies went down four minutes in off "a silly mistake" and let in "three really soft goals" in total. Still, they scored twice and "created a ton".

The hope is they've gotten those issues out of their system with the regular season set to begin on Thursday at Stony Brook.

"So now, instead of learning who we are, it's going to be about learning how to win," Rodriguez said. "We needed those lessons."

UConn's goals are clear. It wants to compete for Big East championships and return to the NCAA Tournament for a second time in three years. The rest of the league believes the Huskies are capable. Now, they need to execute.

"We're being respected in the conference being ranked second but it means nothing. It means absolutely nothing. We gotta learn quickly and come together quickly," Rodriguez said. "Like everyone says, like transfers have experience, but they're still new to a program, no matter who you are, and it takes time to build. During the soccer season, you don't have that much time. You learn on the fly. We know what it takes to get [to the NCAA Tournament], and right now we're working on that."

Among the returners, Glastonbury's Alayna Taylor and Manchester's Se-Hanna Mars should see plenty of time up top, Maree-Anne Van Doesburg impressed as a freshman in the midfield while Lydia LeBlanc will be a lynchpin at left back.

UConn will also be without two of its top players for extended stretches. Midfield Anaya Johnson is dealing with an injury that will likely keep her sidelined until conference play and right back Ines Nourani made Canada's U-20 World Cup roster, which means she'll be gone after the home opener to Rutgers on Aug. 20 and will miss "a big chunk of the season."

Manchester, Connecticut native Shea Boyle (Seton Hall) and Morgan Barry (Vermont) will form UConn's center back pairing.

"They're big, strong and it's just about getting a little bit of continuity and trusting who they are. They're athletic, they're going to protect our net. Love them," Rodriguez said.

Meanwhile, Chloe Shimkin (Texas), "a little spark," will slot in at left wing.

UConn will also rely on a handful of freshmen. Lily Onorato will start in goal — "she's phenomenal," Rodriguez said — while midfielders Maeve Staunton, a native of Bloomfield, and Anya Montano were both highlighted by the coach as "quality" players.

at Stony Brook (Thursday, Aug. 13)

UConn begins the new season tonight at Stony Brook at 6 p.m. ET. The Seawolves were picked to win the CAA in the league's preseason poll.

UConn will open its home slate against former conference mate and perennial NCAA Tournament team Rutgers. The two teams tied 0-0 in Piscataway early last season after the Huskies upset the Scarlet Knights in the first round of the 2024 NCAA Tournament.

This contest will be second half of a doubleheader with UConn men's soccer. Chris Gbandi's squad will take on Syracuse at 5 p.m. ET from Morrone Stadium.

Over the last few years, Brown has quietly established itself as one of the top programs in New England. Between 2021-23, it won three straight Ivy League championships and reached the NCAA Tournament every year. They went 9-4-4 last season.

at St. John's (Wednesday, Sept. 30)

UConn begins Big East play on the final day of September with a trip to St. John's. The Huskies are unbeaten in their last four games against the Red Storm.

Always one of the best teams in the league, Xavier ended UConn's 2025 season with a 7-0 destruction in the Big East Tournament. The Musketeers went on to beat Georgetown in the final and advanced to the second round of the NCAA Tournament.

UConn's arch-nemesis comes to town for senior night on Halloween. Georgetown is the standard in the Big East, having won seven regular season crowns under head coach Dave Nolan while making the NCAA Tournament every season since 2012. The Huskies are just 2-1-8 (W-D-L) against the Hoyas since rejoining the league.

Every Big East game — home and away — will be streamed on ESPN+. The Huskies' home non-conference slate will be available on UConn+ while out-of-conference games on the road will vary depending on the opponent.

title: Carson Beck will not play vs. Raiders due to rib injury
description: Carson Beck impressed in his preseason debut during last week’s Hall of Fame Game.
fullText:
Carson Beck impressed in his preseason debut during last week's Hall of Fame Game.

But his next time on the field will have to wait.

Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Beck will not play in tonight's matchup against the Raiders after suffering a rib injury last Thursday night.

Beck was able to practice all week through soreness from the injury, which is not considered serious. But the team has elected to keep him out of tonight's game as a precaution.

Beck completed 15-of-19 passes for 188 yards with a touchdown against the Panthers last week.

Head coach Mike LaFleur announced earlier this week that Jacoby Brissett and other healthy starters would play against the Raiders. Arizona also has Gardner Minshew and Kedon Slovis on its roster at quarterback.

title: Rays sign INF Jorge Mateo, designate RHP Trevor Martin for assignment
description: Following the loss of infielder Ben Williamson to a likely season ending hamstring strain, the Rays have signed INF Jorge Mateo to a major league deal. Mateo is expected to fill Williamson’s role in the right handed side of a second base platoon role, while also serving as the back up short stop. The move […]
fullText:
Following the loss of infielder Ben Williamson to a likely season ending hamstring strain, the Rays have signed INF Jorge Mateo to a major league deal. Mateo is expected to fill Williamson's role in the right handed side of a second base platoon role, while also serving as the back up short stop. The move also allows rookie Carson Williams to return to Triple-A for every day playing time as he looks to sure up his control of the strike zone against off-speed pitches.

Mateo was released by the Atlanta Braves on August 9th, who signed with them as a free agent following five seasons with the Baltimore Orioles.

To make room on the roster, the Rays have designated RHP Trevor Martin off the 40-man roster, due to right handed relief being the greatest position of depth on the 40-man roster.

Martin made his major league debut this season and pitched 11.1 innings in relief, allowing eight runs (five earned) and four walks against seven strikeouts. In 27 games at the Triple-A level he held a 3.09 ERA and 3.91 FIP with a 25.0% K-rate and 11.2% BB-rate. A third round pick in the 2022 draft, the Rays converted him to starting pitching as a professional from a collegiate relief role, but he has been a relief prospect since the start of the 2025 season. FanGraphs recently rated him No. 40 in the Rays organization pre-2026 draft thanks to his climbing velocity and recent addition of a splitter. He's a big man that will likely find a role elsewhere.

Here is the team's press release:

The Tampa Bay Rays have signed infielder Jorge Mateo (HOR-hay muh-TAY-oh) to a major league contract and recalled right-handed pitcher Jesse Scholtens from Triple-A Durham. To make room on the active and 40-man rosters, the club optioned right-handed pitcher Michael Grove and infielder Carson Williams to Durham and designated right-handed pitcher Trevor Martin for assignment. Mateo will wear No. 9.

Mateo, 31, appeared in 65 games with the Atlanta Braves this season, batting .240/.285/.380 (31-for-129) with six doubles, four home runs, 11 RBI, eight walks, 29 runs scored, and 10 stolen bases on 11 attempts. The right-handed batter hit .316 (25-for-79) with eight extra-base hits and 11 RBI across his first 37 games through the end of May, a stretch he concluded by tallying RBI in each of his final four games to end the month, including consecutive games with a home run for the second time in his career from May 30-31 at Cincinnati. His average sprint speed of 30.3 feet per second leads all major league infielders and ranks third overall behind the Athletics Henry Bolte (30.6) and Texas' Cam Cauley (30.5), according to Baseball Savant. Additionally, Mateo's average arm strength of 88.3 mph is ninth fastest among major league shortstops.

Since the beginning of the 2022 season, the six-foot, 200-pound infielder's 16 defensive runs saved are tied for 11th most among major league shortstops despite playing fewer innings at the position than each of the 10 players ranked ahead of him in that span. Mateo has batted .350 (21-for-60) in 18 career games at Tropicana Field, tallying eight doubles, one triple, five RBI, four walks, nine runs scored, and a .907 OPS. It marks the highest career batting average at the ballpark by any active player (minimum 50 at-bats).

The Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic native signed with the Braves on Jan. 20, was designated for assignment on Aug. 3, and was released on Aug. 9. He spent the previous five seasons (2021-25) with the Baltimore Orioles after the club acquired him from the San Diego Padres ahead of the 2021 trade deadline. In 2022, Mateo became the third player (fourth instance) in Orioles history to lead the American League in steals after swiping a career-high 35 stolen bases, joining Brian Roberts (2007) and Luis Aparicio (1963-64). He began his major league career by playing 22 games with the Padres in 2020.

In 555 career games spanning seven seasons (2020-26), Mateo has slashed .223/.268/.365 (319-for-1,432) with 77 doubles, 12 triples, 34 home runs, 132 RBI, 81 walks, 212 runs scored, and 116 stolen bases.

title: Bucs' A'Shawn Robinson shares his approach in every game
description: A'Shawn Robinson is bringing plenty of intensity to Tampa Bay, explaining why he plans to make things difficult and talk trash on every play.
fullText:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers wanted to bring a different level of intensity to their defense this offseason, and veteran defensive tackle A'Shawn Robinson isn't hiding the mentality he plans to bring with him.

The Pewter Plank's Josh Crysler highlighted Robinson's approach after the veteran spoke with reporters following Sunday's practice. Robinson, who is entering his 11th NFL season, explained that being combative and talking trash are simply part of how he approaches the game.

"It brings tenacity. It brings that fight, that will, that juice, that hunger," Robinson said. "Being combative brings nothing but greatness. So that's all I try to do is make it as tough as I can because I'm going to talk trash every single play."

Robinson added that his approach doesn't change depending on how things are going, saying, "Good or bad, I'm going to talk trash."

That mentality is part of what Tampa Bay added when it signed Robinson this offseason. Crysler pointed to the veteran as a potential source of leadership and accountability for a defense that had questions surrounding both areas last season. Robinson also brings experience from the Los Angeles Rams' Super Bowl-winning team in 2021.

His message isn't only about bringing an edge individually. Robinson emphasized the importance of the entire defense maintaining the same standard and remaining consistent in its actions.

"All we focus on is making sure everybody is locked in, held to the standard, communicating, being consistent, and dominating everything we do," Robinson said. "Leave no stone unturned. Eat everything on your plate."

The Bucs will eventually find out how much Robinson's approach translates once the games begin. What he's bringing to Tampa Bay in the meantime is clear: intensity, accountability and a willingness to make every rep as competitive as possible.

title: Tarp comes off at Field of Dreams as MLB officials hope rain holds off
description: The rain, for now, has stopped. Whether it stays that way is the question hanging over Major League Baseball’s return to the Field of Dreams.
fullText:
DYERSVILLE — The tarp is off. The rain, for now, has stopped.

Whether it stays that way is the question hanging over Major League Baseball's return to the Field of Dreams.

Around 1 p.m. Thursday, Aug. 13, crews began uncovering the diamond at the Dubuque County ballpark after a soggy morning and early afternoon, the first real break from hours of rain ahead of the Minnesota Twins' 6:30 p.m. CT game against the Philadelphia Phillies.

Workers hauled sandbags from the edges of the tarp before lining up across the outfield and wrapping the massive sheet around a long, black corrugated pipe. A swarm of groundskeepers then spread out with leaf blowers and rakes, clearing puddles and working the dirt beneath a gloomy, gray sky.

An MLB staffer told the Register that the tarp came off so crews could begin rehearsals ahead of the game. There was no assurance the break in the weather would last.

"All fingers are crossed," the staffer said.

A round of showers and thunderstorms moved across most of Iowa on Thursday morning, with heavy rain and strong winds among the concerns. Forecasters expected the most widespread rain earlier in the day and some improvement by early afternoon, although scattered showers could linger.

As of shortly after 1 p.m., the rain had stopped at the Field of Dreams Movie Site. But the hourly forecast still called for rain in Dyersville through much of the afternoon and early evening, including around the scheduled first pitch.

The changing conditions were built into Thursday's preparations.

As the grounds crew worked below, the outfield scoreboard cycled through rehearsal messages for an array of possible weather emergencies. One would instruct fans to seek shelter from lightning. Another would tell fans to return to their vehicles if severe weather delayed the opening of the gates. Other test messages covered a weather delay, an evacuation, a cancellation and a postponement of the game until Friday.

title: Celtics predicted to outbid Lakers, Cavs for $46M ex-Warriors NBA champion, pair with Jayson Tatum
description: The Boston Celtics still have some room to add to the roster. They could add one of the Los Angeles Lakers and Cleveland Cavaliers top targets of the summer.
fullText:
Celtics predicted to outbid Lakers, Cavs for $46M ex-Warriors NBA champion, pair with Jayson Tatum originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Jonathan Kuminga's free agency has been one of the biggest storylines of the summer as he continues to search for his next team. His situation has become complicated, particularly with the difficulty of reaching an agreement on a contract.

There has been a clear foundation for Kuminga throughout the summer. From the beginning, the Los Angeles Lakers have been interested in the NBA champion.

"There is mutual free agent interest between Jonathan Kuminga and the Lakers, per Jovan Buha. Los Angeles continues to work behind the scenes to secure Kuminga's commitment as their new wing addition," NBA reporter Evan Sidery wrote.

In fact, the Lakers have been adamant about getting Kuminga into the same offense as Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Currently, the Cleveland Cavaliers and Lakers are believed to be the frontrunners for the 23-year-old star.

"The Lakers and Cavaliers still seem like the most likely landing spots for Kuminga, likely by way of sign-and-trade. The Wolves could be a darkhorse if he wants to take a pay cut, as I don't believe Minnesota will want to acquire him via sign-and-trade, and they are the closest of these teams to getting to the NBA Finals," SI's Jackson Caudell wrote.

While that is the current outlook for Kuminga's potential destinations, Bleacher Report's Dan Favale believes he could ultimately sign with the Boston Celtics.

"Whether Jonathan Kuminga belongs here has little to do with his value as a player. We have yet to see him deliver complementary offense, rebounding and defense for an entire season on top of his from-scratch proclivities, but the physical tools and semi-extended stretches of highest-percentile actualization remain tantalizing. Potential cost is the only barrier for entry. He could be someone that gets more than the $6.1 million mini MLE, particularly if the Atlanta Hawks are willing to facilitate a sign-and-trade," Favale wrote.

This could be a strong opportunity for Kuminga, as the Celtics are looking for another key player to complement Jayson Tatum after trading Jaylen Brown. Boston would also be competing in a jam-packed Eastern Conference.

Kuminga was on a $46 million contract last season. Adding him would give Boston another young, talented piece with plenty of upside. If he can continue developing, Kuminga could become a major part of the Celtics' future and provide a significant boost to their starting lineup.

title: New Reports Reveal Why Newcastle Fell Short in Bruno Guimaraes Transfer
description: Newcastle United may have secured a substantial fee for Bruno Guimaraes, but new reports suggest people from the Magpies organization believe NUFC didn’t actually come out as the winners of the summer-long saga. According to The Athletic, Newcastle’s hierarchy has accepted the club did not get its preferred result even after agreeing to sell the […]
fullText:
Newcastle United may have secured a substantial fee for Bruno Guimaraes, but new reports suggest people from the Magpies organization believe NUFC didn't actually come out as the winners of the summer-long saga.

According to The Athletic, Newcastle's hierarchy has accepted the club did not get its preferred result even after agreeing to sell the Brazil international to Arsenal for a guaranteed £75 million.

"Senior figures at Newcastle accept that Guimaraes leaving and the price they have got for him was not their preferred outcome," The Athletic wrote. "But in this context, the timing and fee are a 'good outcome'."

The Athletic, however, stopped well short of describing the deal as a success.

"Was this a capitulation? No. Was this a rational, necessary decision to conclude negotiations early so they did not repeat the mistakes of last summer? Perhaps," The Athletic wrote. "But a good deal? That feels like a stretch, given how strong Newcastle's stance had been."

The Athletic notes that Newcastle had publicly insisted throughout much of the summer that Guimaraes was not for sale and repeatedly pointed to figures around the £100 million mark. It also points out Lyon will receive around £6-7 million through a 20 percent sell-on clause, reducing the amount Newcastle ultimately keeps from the transfer.

The Telegraph's Luke Edwards has also revealed Arsenal believes it negotiated a bargain deal with Newcastle. According to Edwards, per Chronicle Live's Aaron Morris, the Gunners feel they "saved £25 million" thanks to negotiating the transfer through super agent Kia Joorabchian.

"Andrea Berta's club believe that they have saved £25m on Guimaraes' initial valuation of £100m (by Newcastle), given they are set to fork out a flat guaranteed fee of £75m for the transfer – no add-on clauses included," Morris wrote.

Whether Newcastle genuinely expected to receive £100 million or used that figure as a negotiating tactic remains unclear, but it's true that it got floated at times during the past few weeks, placing Bruno's value on par with the fee Tottenham paid for Sandro Tonali. However, both reports agree the Magpies ultimately accepted less than their original public valuation to bring one of the summer's longest-running transfer sagas to an end.

The focus now shifts toward replacing their former captain, with several midfielders already linked as Matthias Jaissle prepares for his first season at St. James' Park.

Looking back now that the deal is effectively done, do you think Newcastle made the right decision by accepting £75 million for Bruno Guimaraes, or should the club have held firm for more? Share your thoughts in the Coming Home Newcastle comments section below.

title: Report Paredes turned down Milan to stay at Boca Juniors
description: Reports in Argentina claim Milan contacted Leandro Paredes to bring him back to Serie A, but the Argentina international wants to stay at Boca Juniors.The 32-year-old was a regular at the 2026 World C...
fullText:
Reports in Argentina claim Milan contacted Leandro Paredes to bring him back to Serie A, but the Argentina international wants to stay at Boca Juniors.

The 32-year-old was a regular at the 2026 World Cup and reached the Final, which seemingly brought him back to the attention of the Rossoneri.

BUENOS AIRES, ARGENTINA – AUGUST 5: Leandro Paredes of Boca Juniors looks on prior to a Torneo Clausura Mercado Libre 2026 match between Boca Juniors and Estudiantes at Estadio Tomas A. Duco on August 5, 2026 in Buenos Aires, Argentina. (Photo by Marcelo Endelli/Getty Images)

TyC Sports in Argentina report that Milan figures called Paredes over the last few days to ask about his availability, proposing a transfer fee to return him to Italian football.

However, it's suggested he thanked them for their interest, insisting that he was happy with Boca Juniors and had no intention of leaving.

The midfielder has a very long history with Serie A, first coming to Europe with Chievo in 2014, then Empoli and Roma.

After the sale to Zenit St. Petersburg in 2017 and a spell with Paris Saint-Germain, he came back to Italy with Juventus in 2022, then was sold to Roma in 2023.

He went full circle for a return to his first club Boca Juniors in the summer of 2025.

title: Hassan outlines Champions League ambition
description: Newly-signed winger Haissem Hassan says he grew up watching Celtic play in the Champions League and is determined to make the club a regular presence at the top level of European competition.  The 24-year-old, who impressed this summer at the World Cup for Egypt, has joined Martin O'Neill's side as the Champions League play-off first leg with LASK looms next Wednesday.
fullText:
Newly-signed winger Haissem Hassan says he grew up watching Celtic play in the Champions League and is determined to make the club a regular presence at the top level of European competition.

The 24-year-old, who impressed this summer at the World Cup for Egypt, has joined Martin O'Neill's side as the Champions League play-off first leg with LASK looms next Wednesday.

Hassan, whose arrival was followed by fellow new recruit Mika Baur, said through a translator: "Everything is about winning at Celtic, we have to win every game.

"Being in Europe and in the Champions League, because I think Celtic is a club that belongs in the Champions League.

"I've seen them growing up on the TV, and I think we need to go in the Champions League every season.

"I'm here to help the team win trophies, I'm going in the Champions League every year and make the club better season after season."

Hassan has played for clubs in Spain and France, where he was born, and switched his international allegiance to Egypt earlier this year.

The winger is confident he will be able to adapt quickly to the rigours of Scottish football.

"Scottish football might be a bit more tough, but I think at the end that will make me a more complete player," he said.

"I've already done it in France and Spain, so I think I can adapt here as well. At the end, that will be the best for me as well.

"I also play in Africa with Egypt, and that's another style as well. There is no problem for that."

title: Bayern Munich sends Armindo Sieb to Red&Gold partner LAFC
description: FC Bayern is clearing some roster space.
fullText:
Per a release from FCBayern.com, Bayern Munich has shipped attacker Armindo Sieb to Los Angeles FC in MLS.

Sieb, who has had two different stints in Bavaria, is making a permanent move to LAFC:

FC Bayern and Armindo Sieb have agreed on a move for the striker to the 'Red&Gold Football' partner club Los Angeles FC in the USA. The 23-year-old has spent the past two years on loan at FSV Mainz 05.

FC Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund: "Armindo Sieb has gained a great deal of experience in the Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 over the past few years. We are delighted that, following Timothy Tillman, he is now the second player to make the move via our Campus to our 'Red&Gold' partner club, Los Angeles FC. We know he will be in very good hands there and take the next step in his career."

Sieb joined the FC Bayern Campus in the summer of 2020 from the TSG Hoffenheim youth academy and made his professional debut in the DFB Cup in October 2020. After two seasons with SpVgg Greuther Fürth, FC Bayern exercised a buy-back option and handed him a contract until 2027.

LAFC issued the following release on the move as well:

LAFC has acquired forward Armindo Sieb from German Bundesliga club Bayern Munich on a permanent transfer through the 2028-2029 season with a club option through 2029-2030. Sieb will occupy an international roster slot and will be added to the roster pending receipt of his International Transfer Certificate (ITC) and P-1 Visa.

"Armindo is an exciting young player whose technical ability, pace, and attacking prowess will add another dimension to our attack," said LAFC President of Soccer Operations John Thorrington. "He has already gained valuable experience at a young age in one of the world's top footballing environments and has consistently demonstrated the qualities we value in our players. We are excited to welcome Armindo to Los Angeles and believe he will play an important role in our pursuit of championships."

Sieb, 23, joins LAFC after spending the last two seasons on loan with Bundesliga side 1. FSV Mainz 05 from FC Bayern Munich. During his time with Mainz, he made 62 appearances across all competitions, including 49 appearances in the Bundesliga, scoring five goals and adding three assists.

Prior to joining Mainz, Sieb returned to Bayern Munich in the summer of 2024 after the club exercised its buy-back option following his standout two-year spell with 2. Bundesliga club SpVgg Greuther Fürth. He was then loaned to Mainz for the 2024-25 and 2025-26 seasons. During his two seasons with Greuther Fürth, Sieb made 66 appearances across all competitions, recording 17 goals and four assists. In 2023-24, he enjoyed a breakout campaign, contributing 12 goals and three assists in 33 league appearances.

Sieb has always been regarded as a good talent, but he has failed to differentiate himself so far during this preseason. With so many young players warranting longer looks, the writing was on the wall that Sieb might have to move on to have a better chance of showcasing himself.

title: Healthier Tyrese Haliburton Ready For Season, Happy With New Pacers Teammates
description: Indiana Pacers star guard Tyrese Haliburton is finally healthy and ready for another season with new free agents signed.
fullText:
INDIANAPOLIS – Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton can tell you how healthy he is, but he'd rather show you.

In late July, the two-time All-NBA guard took to social media to share some footage of his current athletic level. Haliburton missed the entire 2025-26 NBA season after tearing his right Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, then had his rehab process altered in late February when he was diagnosed with shingles. But now, he looks as good as ever.

The video shows Haliburton training in the Pacers practice facility, the St. Vincent Center. He throws himself a pass by lobbing a basketball in front of him, then runs under it before leaping, grabbing the ball with his left arm and pushing it between his legs, then dunking all before he lands.

"I haven't been able to do that since I was like 20 years old," Haliburton said. That Eastbay Dunk wasn't a spur of the moment decision. Haliburton attempted to pull one off several times during his rehab. He said he missed it on multiple occasions but had a bet with his strength coach that was fairly simple: Make that dunk, and Haliburton could skip his lifting for the day.

"For some reason I just felt good that day," Haliburton said. "I didn't get to miss my lift. I still had to do the lift."

Haliburton has been feeling good for many days recently. He said on Wednesday that he's 100% cleared as it pertains to his Achilles recovery and has no health concerns heading into the coming season. There will still be a ramp up process early in training camp with the Pacers as the former All-Star gets his wind back for game shape, but Haliburton is ready for the coming campaign and will be able to test his explosion against other NBA players soon as he heads out to Los Angeles for some scrimmaging.

"I feel great. I'm doing everything. Playing pickup pretty regularly at this point. So I feel great," Haliburton said. "I will be ready for the season. If the season was today, I'd be ready. So [it] can't come fast enough."

The Pacers first preseason game, as revealed by Haliburton himself, will be on October 7 at Hilton Coliseum in Ames, Iowa. That's where the Iowa State basketball teams play and where Haliburton played his college basketball. It's a special venue for him, both because he played there and got engaged to his now-wife in the arena last summer. And now, it will be the scene for Haliburton's return to action after over 15 months without officially playing.

It will also be the first time he puts on a Pacers uniform alongside some new teammates. This offseason, Indiana added both Kelly Oubre Jr and Larry Nance Jr in free agency, and Ivica Zubac was traded to the franchise back in February.

Haliburton has yet to play with any of them. Nance and Oubre will be new for everyone, but Zubac – who projects to start at center this season – did get some court time for the blue and gold last year. Haliburton shared that he has yet to practice with Zubac this offseason but isn't concerned about that reality. In his eyes, they are both smart players, and Haliburton will make sure they are always on the same team during five-on-five settings during training camp so they can build chemistry.

"I've never played with a screen setter like this. I've never played with a roller like this," Haliburton said of Zubac. "So I'm really looking forward to it, and I think it's gonna be a lot of fun."

Oubre and Nance are the two newest Pacers, at least on standard contracts, and Oubre in particular is a major addition. He projects to be a key reserve for Indiana this season and can play multiple positions. The Pacers' off-ball guard/wing group is now filled with Aaron Nesmith, Andrew Nembhard, Oubre, Jarace Walker, and Ben Sheppard.

That's solid depth, and Oubre's size is a meaningful addition to that crew. He has averaged over 11 points per game in every season since 2017-18 while gradually improving as a shooter and a defender.

Haliburton has connected with Oubre before as they both work with the same trainer, Drew Hanlen. They've worked out and lifted together in the past, so there is already some familiarity there as Oubre joins the Pacers.

"He's a guy who has definitely been annoying for me to go against throughout my career, so I'm excited for him to be on our side," Haliburton began when sharing his opinions on Oubre.

"I think that he adds a lot to us on both sides of the ball, but specifically defensively being able to take on different challenges," he added. Haliburton pointed to the wing depth of the Eastern Conference continuing to improve as a reason that the Oubre addition is so vital for the Pacers. "You're gonna need multiple guys to throw at all these good players. And I think Kelly fits right in with that group."

Nance, meanwhile, projects to be a depth piece on the interior. He has battled injuries in recent seasons and started off the 2025-26 campaign as the backup center for the Cleveland Cavaliers before eventually being replaced in that role. He's been in the league for 11 years and will be a valuable veteran for Indiana.

He averaged 3.7 points and 2.7 rebounds per game last season. "Larry, who's been in the league for a long time, I think he's really gonna be able to help with our frontcourt depth," Haliburton said.

The Pacers have high hopes this season, and Haliburton's health is the biggest factor in that. But their fresh faces and new-look starting five also provide optimism, and Haliburton is a believer in it all. Truly, it's his skillset that brings all different kinds of players together and makes them fit.

Healthy once again, he will try to do so with Zubac, Oubre, Nance, and the rest of the 2026-27 Pacers. And the game action will begin in less than two months.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Aliyah Boston, Kelsey Mitchell latest Fever players to back Stephanie White: 'Our culture is not going to let her fall to the wayside'
description: White has been facing flak for her initial comments about DiJonai Carrington's flagrant 2 foul on Sophie Cunningham and her subsequent address about the WNBA's online discourse.
fullText:
Indiana Fever players continued to go to bat for embattled head coach Stephanie White on Thursday, two days after White was booed at home following her impassioned pregame address to reporters, in which she defended her scrutinized comments about Chicago Sky wing DiJonai Carrington's flagrant 2 foul on Fever guard Sophie Cunningham and called out "the hate, the fear-mongering, the divisiveness" online that she believes is trying to "hijack" the WNBA.

Kelsey Mitchell told media on Thursday that the jeers White received ahead of the Fever's 106-92 win over the New York Liberty at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis threw the four-time All-Star guard for a loop.

"I told her to her face. I said, Coach, this is for you, in terms of just a sense of confidence, a sense of awareness that you're not alone," said Mitchell, a league MVP candidate alongside backcourt partner Caitlin Clark this season, via The Athletic's James Boyd.

"It really hurt my feelings to see her have emotions, in terms of not feeling valued and not feeling wanted in a place where she has to coach. At the end of the day, this is her job. So she has to show up, too. I think that people don't really recognize that. And I think that it's our job to remind her, it's our culture — I think we have to remind her that our culture is not going to let her fall to the wayside."

Mitchell added: "So I hope she knows that."

#Fever’s Kelsey Mitchell on Stephanie White being booed Tuesday:

“If anybody know me, I don’t play that. So, it really hurt my feelings to see her kind of have emotions in terms of not feeling valued, not feeling wanted … Our culture is not gonna let her fall to the wayside.” pic.twitter.com/5B3P6Jrfmt

Aliyah Boston, a four-time All-Star center, described the booing as "really annoying" as well as "disrespectful."

"I think when you are on your home floor and your team's getting announced and the coach is getting announced, I feel like there's no reason for any of that," Boston said, via Boyd.

"I mean, we come out here and we do everything that we can to win. I think Steph does a great job with us. We love her, and we appreciate her. … We kept the main thing the main thing, and we said we're going to come out here and we're going to get that dub."

The Fever followed through, with Mitchell, Boston and Clark combining for 69 points and 11 of the team's 16 3-pointers. As a result, Indiana improved to 21-12, good for the fourth-best record in the W.

#Fever star Aliyah Boston says she felt the “same way” as Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham when Stephanie White was booed Tuesday:

“Steph does a great job with us. We love her, and we appreciate her. So, to hear that, it was really annoying, honestly, and disrespectful. …” pic.twitter.com/iHSHgDRVHb

Following an offensive clinic that included Cunningham going 4 of 5 from deep and finishing a game-high plus-17 off the bench, she emphasized that, despite the "outside noise" facing the Fever, their locker room "is good."

Cunningham, currently at the center of the WNBA's latest controversy after speaking about transgender women in sports, explained that playing, coaching or simply working for the Fever comes with heightened attention and, in turn, distractions.

"But our locker room in there, it's tight, and we have each other's backs. Coach loves us," she said."

White was criticized for the way she initially responded to a postgame question about Carrington's foul on Cunningham this past Saturday. At the time, White praised the effort of Carrington, whom she oversaw in Connecticut as the Sun's head coach from 2023-24, and said that she doesn't "oppose the hard foul." Those remarks weren't received well by a contingent of Fever fans, especially considering Carrington took to social media after her ejection, posting "White Privilege" in all caps and tagging the Fever on Threads.

On Monday, Carrington insisted on X that she "never once claimed that the assessment of the foul was white privilege," however; she did not explain the meaning behind the original post.

On Tuesday, Cunningham referenced White's reasoning that, when she gave her postgame answer about the foul, she hadn't had the chance to watch the replay over and over to adequately judge the severity of the infraction.

"And you know what, DiJonai, she is a hell of a player," Cunningham said. "She's a great defender. And so she coached her for I don't know how many years up in Connecticut. So give her her flowers, and she didn't see it, and that's OK. Me and Steph are great.

"Steph is great with all of us. So it's really the outside noise that's trying to distract us, but we're good."

White ultimately noted on Tuesday that she takes personally "any suggestions that I don't 100% always have my players back."

"I ride with them 10 toes down all the time. All the time," White said.

Clark conveyed on Tuesday how she can relate to White bubbling up. The 24-year-old guard, a three-time All-Star and one of the league's most popular players, sympathized with her head coach, saying that "it's OK to feel those emotions."

"I just told her, I've been through the same thing," Clark said. "There's been days where I've been really upset, and you can have the thickest skin in the world, but sometimes it does get to you. And I think our world is just like … we love to hate, we love to divide — that's all we want to do. Nobody wants to see each other succeed.

"I think that's a really painful thing for myself to watch. I feel like we need to do a better job at uplifting each other."

Clark also underscored on Tuesday that "there was no way we were losing" against the Liberty.

"I hated that our fans booed her before the game," Clark said. "That made me a little sick, to be honest. And you can disagree and this and that. And I get it. It's professional sports, people are going to boo, but at the end of the day, that's our head coach, and we're going to ride for her, and we're always going to have [her] back.

"That's never going to tear our locker room apart. So I just love her, and I feel for her because I know it can be a lot at times."

title: GB teenager Nowacki wins dramatic European gold
description: British teenager Filip Nowacki claims a dramatic gold in the men's 200m breaststroke final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.
fullText:
British teenager Filip Nowacki claimed a dramatic gold in the men's 200m breaststroke final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.

The 18-year-old finished with a late burst in two minutes 7.70 seconds to edge out Dutch swimmer Caspar Corbeau (2:07.78).

Luka Mladenovic of Austria was third (2:08.91), while Briton Gregory Butler finished fifth in 2:09.45.

Nowacki made history for Jersey last month by claiming gold in the 200m breaststroke at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Meanwhile, Lauren Cox and Freya Colbert both won bronze medals for Great Britain.

Cox was third in the women's 50m backstroke final as 19-year-old Italian Sara Curtis won the race in a world record time of 26.56s.

Curtis broke Australian Kaylee McKeown's previous record by 0.23 seconds with a time of 26.63s in the semi- final on Wednesday and improved on that with her victory a day later.

Mary-Ambre Moluh of France was second with 27.06 and Cox was third in 27.15.

Colbert was third, with 1:55.81, in the women's 200m freestyle final as she finished behind winner Barbora Seemanova, who set a championship record of 1:54.38, with Marrit Steenbergen of the Netherlands second in 1:54.65.

title: Jon Rahm may be preparing to leave LIV Golf with potential Ryder Cup decision looming
description: With fines and suspensions reportedly coming on the DP World Tour again, Jon Rahm may be the latest to leave LIV Golf in 2027.
fullText:
Jon Rahm may be preparing an exit from LIV Golf.

There are apparently fears within LIV Golf that Rahm, who is undoubtedly one of the biggest names on the breakaway circuit, will leave after the 2026 campaign, according to The Telegraph's James Corrigan. If that comes to fruition, it would be a massive blow to the venture that is trying to find a way to survive beyond the season.

The DP World Tour is "increasingly confident" that Rahm will return next season, too. According to Corrigan, some believe that the European tour has already been primed about his decision.

It's unclear when Rahm will come to a final decision. LIV Golf is set to hold a tournament in Indianapolis next week. It is widely expected to cancel the team championship in Michigan later this month, too, so next week's tournament will be the final one in the 2026 campaign.

The logistics of Rahm's potential split aren't known, either. He still has multiple years left on the reported $300 million deal he first signed to jump over to LIV Golf in the first place. He even said in May that he didn't "see many ways out" of the contract. But, according to Corrigan, Rahm is still owed a "nine-figure" portion of that deal.

Rahm has won 11 times on the PGA Tour in his career. He picked up his only major championship win at the Masters in 2023, though the former top-ranked golfer in the world finished in second at the PGA Championship earlier this year. He's won multiple times with LIV Golf this season, too.

Things aren't solidified just yet, but the breakup between Rahm and LIV would make sense for a number of reasons.

First, LIV Golf's future has been incredibly murky after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced earlier this year it would no longer fund the league after the season. That sent the league into turmoil, and left CEO Scott O'Neil and others scrambling to find new financial backers.

LIV announced earlier this month that it had secured an unnamed "lead investor" to find the league for years to come, but specifics were not announced. The name of the investor was kept quiet, too. LIV also announced that golfers would be able to own equity in the league. But Rahm, according to Corrigan, "is not enamored by the prospect of the new LIV iteration."

Then on Wednesday, the DP World Tour reportedly started notifying LIV Golf members that it would resume imposing heavy fines and suspensions as part of its conflicting events rule in 2027. That essentially was the European league drawing a line in the sand and forcing LIV Golf members to choose between them and LIV Golf after it had allowed conditional releases for members to play in this season. Rahm had struck a deal to pay off his fines and resume playing with the DP World Tour this season after a long feud.

Had Rahm not reached that deal, he would have lost his DP World Tour membership and been ineligible for the Ryder Cup in 2027. That league controls the European team, and members must be in good standing with the Tour in order to participate in next year's competition in Ireland. If Rahm ends up staying with LIV Golf next season, his status for the European Ryder Cup team next fall will absolutely be in doubt.

It's unclear where the PGA Tour stands with Rahm. It could force Rahm to serve a one-year suspension, like Patrick Reed had to, in order to return. Or it could offer him a path back like it did with Brooks Koepka earlier this year, which came with heavy fines and restrictions.

But regardless of the specifics or the reasoning, LIV Golf losing Rahm would be just the latest blow for the league this season. Rahm is arguably the biggest name left with LIV Golf, behind only Bryson DeChambeau. Losing him would not only take more eyes away, but would make a pitch to potential new financial backers that much harder to sell.

title: Cerebras stock plunges 14% after second earnings report following IPO
description: Cerebras Systems reported better-than-expected second-quarter revenue and raised its full-year guidance.
fullText:
Cerebras Systems raised its full-year guidance in the second earnings report following the chipmaker's initial public offering in May. But the stock tumbled about 14% in extended trading.

Here's how it did in the second quarter versus LSEG consensus estimates:

Cerebras said in a statement on Wednesday that it expects core revenue of between $214 million and $216 million this quarter.

The company raised its full-year outlook and now expects core revenue of between $880 million and $890 million, up from a prior range of $855 million to $865 million.

The $180 million sales figure for the second quarter represents total revenue. Cerebras also reported a core revenue figure of $210 million, which strips out the impact from "pass-through revenue" and "amortization of customer warrant assets."

The company recorded a net loss of $450.5 million, after finishing with a profit of $309.5 million, or $1.91 per share, a year earlier. Most of the loss is tied to stock-compensation costs of $386.6 million.

Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman said in an interview that AI demand is "through the roof" and that companies are paying up for its specialty inference chips.

Cerebras is challenging AI chip leader Nvidia for some AI tasks, especially those that need "low latency," or quick responses for interactivity. The company calls it "fast inference." The company said its core gross margin will expand to between 38% and 40% in the current quarter, addressing a concern for investors.

"Gross margins are are in a good spot, and growing, because fast inference is priced at a premium," Feldman said in an interview, adding that Cerebras was able to increase the AI output of its systems.

Cerebras went public on the Nasdaq in May, capitalizing on investor interest in semiconductors that can run AI models. It priced its offering at $185 and raised $6.4 billion in the offering. The stock peaked in May and has fallen since, but closed on Wednesday at $262.06, up 42% from its IPO.

The chipmaker has $25.4 billion in remaining performance obligations, which it said was a sign of "extraordinary future demand." Feldman said that as Cerebras grows, it will benefit from larger scale. The company also said it expects revenue to triple in the next fiscal year.

"We will manufacture more efficiently. We'll get better pricing on componentry. We'll amortize our manufacturing organization over more units," Feldman said. "All of those point up and to the right."

In recent weeks, Cerebras announced a partnership with Nvidia rival Advanced Micro Devices, with products going into production later this year, and said that OpenAI can use its chips to serve its latest model, GPT 5.6 Sol. Cerebras also offers access to its chips through its cloud, which reported $126 million in revenue during the June quarter.

WATCH: Cerebras sees OpenAI's chip competing with other GPUs

Correction: An earlier version of this story incorrectly identified what is included in core revenue.

title: Stein's Paradox and What Partial Pooling Can Do for You (2019)
description: In many instances, partial pooling leads to better estimates than taking simple averages will, a finding sometimes called Stein's Paradox. In 1977, Efron and Morris published a great paper discussing the phenomenon. In this post, I'll walk out Efron and Morris's baseball example and then link it to contemporary Bayesian multilevel models.
fullText:
Sometimes a mathematical result is strikingly contrary to generally held belief even though an obviously valid proof is given. 
Charles Stein of Stanford University discovered such a paradox in statistics in 1955. His result undermined a century and a half of work on estimation theory. (
Efron & Morris, 1977, p. 119)
The James-Stein estimator leads to better predictions than simple means. Though I don’t recommend you actually use the James-Stein estimator in applied research, understanding why it works might help clarify why it’s time social scientists consider 
defaulting to multilevel models for their work-a-day projects.

I recently noticed someone—I wish I could recall who—tweet about Efron and Morris’s classic paper, 
Stein’s paradox in statistics. At the time, I was vaguely aware of the paper but hadn’t taken the chance to read it. The tweet’s author mentioned how good a read it was. Now I’ve finally given it a look, I concur. I’m not a sports fan, but I really appreciated their primary example using batting averages from baseball players in 1970. It clarified why partial pooling leads to better estimates than taking simple averages.

In this post, I’ll walk out Efron and Morris’s baseball example and then link it to contemporary Bayesian multilevel models.

For this project, I’m presuming you are familiar with logistic regression, vaguely familiar with the basic differences between frequentist and Bayesian approaches to fitting regression models, and have heard of multilevel models. All code in is 
R (
R Core Team, 2022), with a heavy use of the 
tidyverse (
Wickham et al., 2019; 
Wickham, 2022), and the 
brms package for Bayesian regression (
Bürkner, 2017, 
2018, 
2022).

Stein’s paradox concerns the use of observed averages to estimate unobservable quantities. Averaging is the second most basic process in statistics, the first being the simple act of counting. A baseball player who gets seven hits in 20 official times at bat is said to have a batting average of .350. In computing this statistic we are forming an estimate of the payer’s true batting ability in terms of his observed average rate of success. Asked how well the player will do in his next 100 times at bat, we would probably predict 35 more hits. In traditional statistical theory it can be proved that no other estimation rule is uniformly better than the observed average.

The paradoxical element in Stein’s result is that it sometimes contradicts this elementary law of statistical theory. If we have three or more baseball players, and if we are interested in predicting future batting averages for each of them, then there is a procedure that is better than simply extrapolating from the three separate averages…

As our primary data we shall consider the batting averages of 18 major-league players as they were recorded after their first 45 times at bat in the 1970 season. (
Efron & Morris, 1977, p. 119)
Let’s enter the baseball data.

Here’s what those data look like.

We have data from 18 players. The main columns are of the number of hits for their first 45 times_at_bat. I got the player, hits, and times_at_bat values directly from the paper. However, Efron and Morris didn’t include the batting averages for the end of the season in the paper. Happily, I was able to find those values in the 
online posting of the first chapter of one of Effron’s books (
2010) . They’re included in the true_ba column.

These were all the players who happened to have batted exactly 45 times the day the data were tabulated. A batting average is defined, of course, simply as the number of hits divided by the number of times at bat; it is always a number between 0 and 1. (
Efron & Morris, 1977, p. 119)
I like use a lot of plots to better understand what I’m doing. Before we start plotting, I should point out the color theme in this project comes from 
here. [Haters gonna hate.]

We might use a histogram to get a sense of the hits.

Here is the distribution of the end-of-the-season batting averages, true_ba.

For each of the 18 players in the data, our goal is to the best job possible to use the data for their first 45 times at bat (i.e., hits and times_at_bat) to predict their batting averages at the end of the season (i.e., true_ba). Before Charles Stein, the conventional reasoning was their initial batting averages (i.e., hits / times_at_bat) are the best way to do this. It turns out that would be naïve. To see why, let

The first step in applying Stein’s method is to determine the average of the averages. Obviously this grand average, which we give the symbol \(\overline y\), must also lie between 0 and 1. The essential process in Stein’s method is the “shrinking” of all the individual averages toward this grand average. If a player’s hitting record is better than the grand average, then it must be reduced; if he is not hitting as well as the grand average, then his hitting record must be increased. The resulting shrunken value for each player we designate \(z\). (
Efron & Morris, 1977, p. 119)
As such, the James-Stein estimator is

$$z = \overline y + c(y - \overline y),$$

where, in the paper, \(c = .212\). Let’s get some of those values into the baseball data.

Which set of values, \(y\) or \(z\), is the better indicator of batting ability for the 18 players in our example? In order to answer that question in a precise way one would have to know the “true batting ability” of each player. This true average we shall designate \(\theta\) (the Greek letter theta). Actually it is an unknowable quantity, an abstraction representing the probability that a player will get a hit on any given time at bat. Although \(\theta\) is unobservable, we have a good approximation to it: the subsequent performance of the batters. It is sufficient to consider just the remainder of the 1970 season, which includes about nine times as much data as the preliminary averages were based on. (
Efron & Morris, 1977, p. 119)
Now we have both \(y\) and \(z\) in the data, let’s compare their distributions.

As implied in the formula, the James-Stein estimates are substantially shrunken towards the grand mean, y_bar. To get a sense of which estimate is better, we can subtract the estimate from theta, the end of the season batting average.

Since y_error and y_error are error distributions, we prefer values to be as close to zero as possible. Let’s take a look.

The James-Stein errors (i.e., z_error) are more concentrated toward zero. In the paper, we read: “One method of evaluating the two estimates is by simply counting their successes and failures. For 16 of the 18 players the James-Stein estimator \(z\) is closer than the observed average \(y\) to the ‘true,’ or seasonal, average \(\theta\)” (pp. 119–121). We can compute that with a little ifelse().

A more quantitative way of comparing the two techniques is through the total squared error of estimation… The observed averages \(y\) have a total squared error of .077, whereas the squared error of the James-Stein estimators is only .022. By this comparison, then, Stein’s method is 3.5 times as accurate. (
Efron & Morris, 1977, p. 121)

We can get the 3.5 value with simple division.

So it does indeed turn out that shrinking each player’s initial estimate toward the grand mean of those initial estimates does a better job of predicting their end-of-the-season batting averages than using their individual batting averages. To get a sense of what this looks like, let’s make our own version of the figure on page 121.

The James-Stein estimator works because of its shrinkage, and the shrinkage factor is called \(c\). Though in the first parts of the paper, Efron and Morris just told us \(c = .212\), they gave the actual formula for \(c\) a little later on. If you let \(k\) be the number of means (i.e., the number of clusters), then

$$c = 1 - \frac{(k - 3)\sigma^2}{\sum (y - \overline y)^2}.$$

The difficulty of that formula is we don’t know the value for \(\sigma^2\). It’s not the sample variance of \(y\) (i.e., var(y)). An 
answer to this stackexchange question helped clarify Efron and Morris were using the formula for the standard error of the estimate,

$$\sqrt{\hat p(1 - \hat p) / n},$$

which, in the variance metric, is simply

Following along, we can compute sigma_squared like so:

Now we can reproduce the \(c\) value from the paper.

This has been fun. But I don’t recommend you actually use the James-Stein estimator in your research.

The James-Stein estimator is not the only one that is known to be better than the sample averages…

The search for new estimators continues. Recent efforts [in the 1970s, that is] have been concentrated on achieving results like those obtained with Stein’s method for problems involving distributions other than the normal distribution. Several lines of work, including Stein’s and Robbins’ and more formal Bayesian methods seem to be converging on a powerful general theory of parameter estimation. (
Efron & Morris, 1977, p. 127, emphasis added)
The James-Stein estimator is not Bayesian, but it is a precursor to the kind of analyses we now do with Bayesian multilevel models, which pool cluster-level means toward a grand mean. To get a sense of this, we’ll fit a couple models. First, let’s load the brms package.

I typically work with the linear regression paradigm. If we were to analyze the baseball data, we’d use an aggregated binomial mode, which is a particular kind of logistic regression. You can learn more about it 
here. If we wanted a model that corresponded to the \(y\) estimates, above, we’d use hits as the criterion and allow each player to get his own separate estimate. Since we’re working within the Bayesian paradigm, we also need to assign priors. In this case, we’ll use a weakly-regularizing \(\operatorname{Normal}(0, 1.5)\) on the intercepts. See 
this wiki for more on weakly-regularizing priors.

Here’s the code to fit the model with brms.

If you were curious, that model followed the statistical formula

$$
\begin{align*} \text{hits}_i & \sim \operatorname{Binomial} (n = 45, p_i) \\ \operatorname{logit}(p_i) & = \alpha_\text{player} \\ \alpha_\text{player} & \sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 1.5), \end{align*}
$$

where \(p_i\) is the probability of player \(i\), \(\alpha_\text{player}\) is a vector of \(\text{player}\)-specific intercepts from within the logistic regression model, and each of those intercepts are given a \(\operatorname{Normal}(0, 1.5)\) prior on the log-odds scale. (If this is all new and confusing, don’t worry. I’ll recommended some resources at the end of this post.)

For our analogue to the James-Stein estimate \(z\), we’ll fit the multilevel version of that last model. While each player still gets his own estimate, those estimates are now partially-pooled toward the grand mean.

That model followed the statistical formula

$$
\begin{align*} \text{hits}_i & \sim \operatorname{Binomial}(n = 45, p_i) \\ \operatorname{logit}(p_i) & = \alpha + \alpha_\text{player} \\ \alpha & \sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 1.5) \\ \alpha_\text{player} & \sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, \sigma_\text{player}) \\ \sigma_\text{player} & \sim \operatorname{HalfNormal}(0, 1.5), \end{align*}
$$

where \(\alpha\) is the grand mean among the \(\text{player}\)-specific intercepts, \(\alpha_\text{player}\) is the vector of \(\text{player}\)-specific deviations from the grand mean, which are Normally distributed with a mean of zero and a standard deviation of \(\sigma_\text{player}\), which is estimated from the data.

If you’re new to aggregated binomial or logistic regression, those estimates might be confusing. For technical reasons–see 
here–, they’re in the log-odds metric. But we can use the brms::inv_logit_scaled() function to convert them back to a probability metric. Why would we want a probability metric?, you might ask. As it turns out, batting average is in a probability metric, too. So you might also think of the inv_logit_scaled() function as turning the model results into a batting-average metric. For example, if we wanted to get the estimated batting average for E. Rodriguez based on the y_fit model (i.e., the model corresponding to the \(y\) estimator), we might do something like this.

To double check the model returned a sensible estimate, here’s the corresponding y value from the baseball data.

It’s a little off, but in the right ballpark. Here is the corresponding estimate from the multilevel model, fit_z.

And indeed that’s pretty close to the z value from the baseball data, too.

So now we have these too competing ways to model the data of the first 45 times at bat, let’s see how well their estimates predict the true_ba values. We’ll do so with a couple plots. This first one is of the single-level model which did not pool the batting averages.

Note our use of some handy convenience functions (i.e., add_fitted_draws() and stat_interval()) from the 
tidybayes package (
Kay, 2022).

This second plot is almost the same as the previous one, but this time based on the partial-pooling multilevel model.

Here we join them together with patchwork (
Pedersen, 2022).

In both panels, the end-of-the-season batting averages (i.e., \(\theta\)) are the blue dots. The model-implied estimates are depicted by 95% and 50% interval bands (i.e., the lighter and darker green horizontal lines, respectively). The white line in the background marks off the mean of \(\theta\). Although neither model was perfect, the multilevel model, our analogue to the James-Stein estimates, yielded predictions that appear both more valid and more precise.

We might also compare the models by their prediction errors. Here we’ll subtract the end-of-the-season batting averages from the model estimates. But unlike with y and z estimates, above, our fit_y and fit_z models yielded entire posterior distributions. Therefore, we’ll express our prediction errors in terms of error distributions, rather than single values.

For consistency, I’ve ordered the players along the \(y\)-axis the same as above. In both panels, we see the prediction error distribution for each player in green and then summarize those distributions in terms of their means and percentile-based 95% intervals. Since these are error distributions, we prefer them to be as close to zero as possible. Although neither model made perfect predictions, the overall errors in the multilevel model were clearly smaller. Much like with the James-Stein estimator, the partial pooling of the multilevel model made for better end-of-the-season estimates.

The paradoxical [consequence of Bayesian multilevel models] is that [they can contradict] this elementary law of statistical theory. If we have [two] or more baseball players, and if we are interested in predicting future batting averages for each of them, then [the Bayesian multilevel model can be better] than simply extrapolating from [the] separate averages. (
Efron & Morris, 1977.), p. 119]
This is another example of how the 
KISS principle isn’t always the best bet with data analysis.

If you’re new to logistic regression, multilevel models or Bayesian statistics, I recommend any of the following texts:

If you choose Statistical rethinking, do check out 
these great lectures on the text.

Also, don’t miss the provocative (
2017) preprint by Davis-Stober, Dana and Rouder, 
When are sample means meaningful? The role of modern estimation in psychological science.

Bürkner, P.-C. (2017). brms: An R package for Bayesian multilevel models using Stan. Journal of Statistical Software, 80(1), 1–28. 
https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v080.i01

Bürkner, P.-C. (2018). Advanced Bayesian multilevel modeling with the R package brms. The R Journal, 10(1), 395–411. 
https://doi.org/10.32614/RJ-2018-017

title: HN: Xenon, open source dashboard for a second screen, tablet or phone
description: A spare monitor, a tablet or the phone in your pocket becomes one touch dashboard: monitor, media, voice AI, file transfer, Deck. Free, open source, and it runs on your PC. No cloud, no account, no telemetry.
fullText:
Seven of the areas it covers; the full list of widgets is further down.

Say "Hey Xenon" and it answers, through Gemini, ChatGPT or Claude, or through Ollama on the same PC.

A grid of programmable keys that open apps, switch OBS scenes, send hotkeys and webhooks, or drive Discord voice and Spotify.

CPU, GPU, RAM, network and the real in-game frame rate, kept for thirty days.

Pull the top bar down and type the way you would say it, like "photos from december", and it searches an index that lives on your own disk.

Open a drive and the map is already drawn, because the index behind it is kept current in the background instead of rebuilt on demand. Cleanup proposes only what is on a fixed list of caches and temporary files, and what it removes goes to the Recycle Bin.

Vitals watches hydration, focus and posture, but only if you switch it on, and Bit is the pixel pet that keeps asking until you take the break.

Hue, WLED, Govee, LIFX, Nanoleaf and your CORSAIR gear, driven by CPU temperature, album art or a timer running out.

See the full list of what's in there

Themes, backgrounds, widgets and whole packs made by other users. Copy a code, paste it into Xenon and it is applied.
