title: Nero’s Bridge emerges from Tiber River as Rome faces water crisis
description: The remains of an ancient bridge have emerged in Rome’s Tiber River, near St. Peter’s Basilica, as weeks with virtually no rain caused water levels to plunge.  The bridge — known as Nero's Bridge, nam...
fullText:
ROME (AP) — The remains of an ancient bridge have emerged in Rome's Tiber River, near St. Peter's Basilica, as weeks with virtually no rain caused water levels to plunge.

The bridge — known as Nero's Bridge, named for the former Roman emperor — once connected Rome's city center with the Tiber's right bank.

"Nero is the most famous person linked to this area, because precisely in Nero's circus, where the Vatican is now located, the Apostle Peter was martyred," said Antonella Bonini, an archaeologist at Rome's cultural heritage superintendency.

"However, scholars consider the bridge to be older (than Nero's era) — built by Caligula, Nero's uncle," she said, adding that it existed as early as 39 AD.

The Tiber's flow has fallen below 80 cubic meters (2,825 cubic feet) per second, about half the historic average for the month of July, according to Giovanni Giganti, coordinator of the Rome civil protection service's center for water management.

"We are facing a major water crisis. And it is a crisis that is also due to the fact that this winter we did have quite abundant rainfall, but then the dry periods ... were quite long," Giganti said.

title: Astronomy superfan, 11, shares tips for watching solar eclipse
description: Efan Dafydd's love of the cosmos continued to grow after meeting his hero, astronaut Tim Peake.
fullText:
Space superfan Efan Dafydd has loved astronomy since he was just two years old.

His mum, Lowri, gave him a Welsh-language book called Gofod, which means space.

The avid stargazer has warned people ahead of Wednesday's partial solar eclipse not to rely on special glasses used during the total eclipse in 1999.

"[They] are not suitable because they could be scratched or damaged, which could make you lose your vision," he said.

The budding astronaut has received tips on realising his dream from hero Tim Peake - and has even started learning Russian.

On Wednesday, the UK and parts of Europe will experience the most significant solar eclipse in almost three decades.

More than 90% of the Sun will be covered by the Moon for most of the UK, the largest solar eclipse visible until September 2090.

The event will begin at approximately 18:10 BST, although timings will vary depending on location.

Efan, a member of the Vale Stargazing Club, reminded people that "normal sunglasses won't work" when it comes to watching the event, saying that special solar glasses are needed.

"And if you're taking pictures with your phone or looking through a telescope or binoculars, you have to get a solar filter… because the UV light can destroy the lens," he said.

Speaking about seeing his first solar eclipse, which he plans to view on the runway of a gliding club in Denbigh, Efan said he thought it might get "really cold" when it happens, but it was a "really exciting opportunity".

Efan said the "coolest" thing he had seen while stargazing was Jupiter because "it was just so clear", but that his favourite planet was Neptune because of its Great Dark Spot, a vast storm system roughly the size of Earth.

In October, Efan met his hero, retired British European Space Agency astronaut Peake, during a book tour event after waiting "outside on the backstage door".

It was at this meeting that Peake told Efan the practical steps on how to achieve his dream of becoming an astronaut.

They included getting an engineering degree or a Royal Air Force route, but also to "do good in school" and "stay fit and healthy".

To further increase his chances, Efan was advised to learn Russian because it can help facilitate training at the Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center in Russia, according to The European Space Agency.

He is currently on an almost 300-day Duolingo streak, and has learnt to say greetings like "good morning", familial relations and animals like dogs and cats.

title: Berrington & Robertson star as Scotland crush Canada
description: Captain Richie Berrington and debutant Lyle Robertson star as Scotland enjoy a thumping 170-run World Cup League 2 victory over Canada at Forthill.
fullText:
ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 tri-series, Forthill

Scotland 347-7 (50 overs): Berrington 120, McMullen 64, Cross 51, Jones 41; Shirzad 4-60

Canada 177 (35 overs): P. Singh 42; Robertson 6-52

Captain Richie Berrington and debutant Lyle Robertson starred as Scotland enjoyed a thumping 170-run Cricket World Cup League 2 victory over Canada at Forthill.

Berrington, 39, hit an impressive 120 as the hosts posted an imposing total of 347 from their 50 overs before Falkland off-spinner Robertson ripped through Canada's batting order, taking six wickets for 52 runs.

Berrington's seventh one-day international century included four sixes, taking his overall haul to 90 - a new Scottish record, overtaking George Munsey's 87.

Brandon McMullen (64) shared a third-wicket partnership of 140 with his captain after the departure of openers Finlay McCreath and Michael English had Scotland on 25-2 in the seventh over.

Michael Jones and Matthew Cross kept up the brisk run rate with knocks of 41 and 51 not out respectively and Jack Jarvis added 30 from 14 balls for a 347-7 total.

Berrington was also involved as Canada lost their first wicket in the third over of their reply, taking a catch from the bowling of Mark Watt.

Pargat Singh (42) was the only Canadian batter to offer any meaningful resistance as Robertson staked his claim for a regular place in the Scotland side.

The 23-year-old picked up his first international wicket as Harsh Thaker picked out Oliver Davidson on the midwicket boundary and his day got even better as he took five scalps from his final 15 deliveries to finish with remarkable figures.

After dismissing Shreyas Movva and Zahid Shirzad in successive balls for his five-wicket haul, Robertson had number 11 Kaleem Sana in his sights for a hat-trick.

That particular feat was not to be, but Robertson ripped one back through bat and pad with the last ball of his spell to seal a massive win and cap a dream debut.

Scotland were already assured of place in the World Cup qualifier after last week's win over the same opponents.

Having beaten the United Arab Emirates on Sunday, the defending champions are now top of the World Cup League 2 standings, although they have played four more matches than the United States, who sit two points behind.

title: Four Canadian hockey stars remain suspended after sexual assault acquittal
description: A fifth has been reinstated, though an appeals board found that the whole group broke Hockey Canada's code of conduct.
fullText:
Four ice hockey players who were acquitted of sexual assault last year should remain barred from representing Canada at international level because they broke Hockey Canada's code of conduct, an independent appeals board has ruled.

The board recommended that four of the five acquitted players remain suspended from all Hockey Canada-sanctioned programmes.

The fifth player, Alex Formenton, was also deemed to have broken conduct rules, but is now being reinstated.

The former players for Canada's under-20s junior hockey team were accused of sexual assault over an incident that took place in 2018. They were found not guilty in July 2025.

The players are Michael McLeod, Dillon Dube, Cal Foote and Carter Hart, as well as Formenton.

The ruling does not change the fact that all five players are eligible to play for teams that compete in the National Hockey League (NHL), which operates separately from Hockey Canada.

All five were allowed by the NHL to sign contracts again for the league's teams late last year. The NHL operates under a separate authority to Hockey Canada, and conducted its own investigation into the incident that was at the centre of the legal case.

While Forementon is eligible for immediate reinstatement by Hockey Canada, the others will have to wait for months or years before they can return to the ice at an international level.

Foote will be eligible on 10 November of this year, while Hart and Dube will be eligible on 10 November 2027 and 10 November 2028 respectively. McLeod will have to wait until 10 November 2030.

Officials did not say why the reinstatement dates differed for each player.

Five ice hockey players found not guilty in Canada sexual assault case

The players had been accused of assaulting the woman, known as EM, in a hotel room in 2018 in London, Ontario, where they had been attending a gala.

They were acquitted in July 2025 when Justice Maria Carroccia said she did not find EM's evidence "credible or reliable".

The court heard that the woman had met the players at a bar and later went back to the hotel room to have consensual sex with McLeod. Other players then entered the room and engaged in further sexual acts with her.

The central issue of the trial was whether EM, who was 20 at the time of the incident, had consented to every sexual act in the hotel room that night.

Lawyers for the players contended that EM asked the men to have sex with her and they believed she gave consent.

EM, however, testified that she was intoxicated and felt fearful of the men. While she had initially agreed to have sex with McLeod, she testified that she did not agree to what unfolded afterwards.

Despite the fact that the incident happened eight years ago, the case remains on the minds of many in Canada.

"This case started a national conversation about safe sport and the problematic culture in men's hockey," said Adam van Koeverden, Canada's current secretary of sport, in a statement after the Wednesday's ruling by the appeals board.

"It is the voices of women and survivors, and the courage and bravery it takes to come forward, that have led to changes we are seeing in toxic culture."

Van Koeverden said there has been progress at Hockey Canada to "address long-standing systemic failures" and said that national sport organisations must be held accountable.

title: Why half of England's World Cup defenders are on the move
description: England came third in this summer's World Cup - their best performance in a men's competition in 60 years - and now their players are in demand in the transfer market.
fullText:
England came third in this summer's World Cup - their best performance in a men's competition in 60 years - and now their players are in demand in the transfer market.

Of the 27 players that went out to North America - 26 in the original squad and Trevoh Chalobah, who replaced the injured Tino Livramento - seven have moved clubs this summer, with another two linked with transfers.

Morgan Rogers went from Aston Villa to Chelsea in a £117m deal, midfielder Elliot Anderson moved for £116m from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City and winger Anthony Gordon cost Barcelona almost £70m when transferring from Newcastle.

Midfielder Jordan Henderson made the short trip across west London on a free transfer to Chelsea after his Brentford contract was mutually terminated and back-up goalkeeper James Trafford signed for Leeds in a £45m move from Manchester City.

But what might be more surprising is how in-demand England's defenders have become - and the low prices they are moving for.

With Djed Spence on the verge of going to Inter Milan, where he could join Three Lions team-mate John Stones, Trevoh Chalobah having moved to Como and Ezri Konsa being targeted by Arsenal, four of England's World Cup defenders will be potentially moving clubs this summer.

But if you go back a bit further, Marc Guehi left Crystal Palace for Manchester City in January and Jarell Quansah moved from Liverpool to Bayer Leverkusen in July 2025 - meaning six of the nine England defenders on World Cup duty could have switched teams in just over a year.

We look at the defenders on the move this summer and explain why they are moving; the push and pull factors involved and what the moves will offer both the player and the clubs involved.

Although attacking players such as Rogers and Gordon and central midfielder Anderson have been involved in massive deals this summer, there has certainly been more value to be found in the defenders.

Tottenham full-back Spence, 26, might only cost Inter Milan £25.6m, despite ending the World Cup strongly, repeatedly displaying his pace and willingness to go forward.

He impressed in the semi-final, including a superb last-ditch sliding challenge to stop Argentina's Giuliano Simeone from scoring.

Spurs finished 17th last season, only clinching Premier League survival on the final day, while Inter Milan are the reigning Serie A champions and also Coppa Italia holders.

Stones, 32, was always going to be in demand as he was available on a free transfer after a hugely-successful spell at Manchester City, winning the Premier League six times and the Champions League once.

The only question was over his fitness, but he answered those worries by featuring in five of England's eight World Cup matches, having played in all five in 2022 and all seven in 2018, when the Three Lions again lost in the semi-finals.

He has played 94 times for England and was also an ever-present in their runs to the European Championship finals in 2021 and 2024 and seems to be a risk-free bargain for Inter.

Konsa, 28, played in all eight World Cup matches this summer, with Arsenal failing with a bid of £30m and Villa holding out for near double that.

But even a transfer of under £50m would prove good value for a player that has played 28 times for his country and helped Villa win the Europa League in May.

Arsenal won the Premier League in 2025-26 and reached the final of the Champions League, but with France centre-half William Saliba set to miss an "extended period" because of a back injury, they are in need for an instant high-level replacement, which Konsa would be.

Chalobah, 27, only featured in the third-fourth play-off, which England won 6-4 against France in a crazy game in Miami as he earned his second international cap.

However, his transfer to Italian side Como, who are managed by ex-Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas and qualified for the Champions League for the first time in their history, still comes in at the cheaper end of the market.

Chelsea will receive an initial £25.7m, with a further £5.1m possible in add-ons, while France defender Maxence Lacroix, signed from Crystal Palace, cost the Blues much more at £52m.

Chalobah had been at Chelsea since the age of eight, winning the FA Cup, Conference League and Fifa Club World Cup twice - playing all 90 minutes of the final as the Blues beat Paris St-Germain 3-0 in 2025.

But with the arrival of Lacroix and with numerous other central defensive options, including Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Axel Disasi, Tosin Adarabioyo, Benoit Badiashile and Jorrel Hato, Chalobah has opted for more guaranteed first-team football.

Guehi, 26, another who played in all of England's World Cup games, only cost Manchester City £20m in January as his Crystal Palace contract was expiring in six months.

It was a similar story for right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold, surprisingly left out of Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad after a season at Real Madrid, who only paid Liverpool £8.5m in May 2025 with his Anfield deal coming to an end.

The most expensive move among the names mentioned was Quansah's £35m move from Liverpool to Bayer Leverkusen last summer, although the fact he was only 22 at the time was one of the reasons for the German side paying more.

In the past eight years, England have reached two World Cup semi-finals, one quarter-final and the final of two European Championships.

Firstly under Gareth Southgate and then under Thomas Tuchel, the Three Lions have generally been well organised, hard to break down and tough to beat - with defensive players being able to shine.

When they finished fourth in the 2018 World Cup, they conceded only eight goals in seven games and it was the same figures in 2026 in their opening seven matches, before the madness of the 6-4 win over France.

They only conceded twice in seven games in the European Championship in 2021 and six in seven matches at Euro 2024, losing in the final on both occasions.

Under Tuchel, England did not concede a single goal in qualifying for the 2026 World Cup, winning all eight qualifiers and keeping clean sheets in all of them to get to North America with a maximum 24 points.

An attacking and exciting 4-2 win over Croatia in their 2026 opener, led to many thinking there had been a change of philosophy, before England then kept two clean sheets in a row in their other group matches.

England's resolute defending was typified in the last-16 3-2 win over co-hosts Mexico, with Tuchel's side hanging on, despite playing the final 40 minutes with 10 men after Quansah had been sent off.

Similar defensive qualities saw off Norway and star striker Erling Haaland in the quarter-finals, but they could not repeat the trick late on in their semi-final when Argentina, inspired by Lionel Messi, scored twice late on to end English hopes of glory.

title: Tielemans apologises to Villa fans for Man Utd remarks
description: Youri Tielemans apologises to Aston Villa fans after suggesting he had moved to a bigger club in Premier League rivals Manchester United.
fullText:
Youri Tielemans has apologised to Aston Villa fans after suggesting he had moved to a bigger club in Premier League rivals Manchester United.

The Belgium midfielder, 29, moved to Old Trafford this summer on a five-year deal from Villa when United triggered a £35m release clause in his contract.

Tielemans spent three years at Villa Park after joining from Leicester City in 2023, making 134 appearances and scoring 10 goals.

Speaking during United's pre-season tour, Tielemans praised Villa for putting him "back to my best level", before adding: "But there are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them."

Some Villa fans were unhappy with Tielemans' comments, so he took to Instagram, external to clear the air.

"Never meant for my words in the press yesterday to offend anyone or the institution of Aston Villa Football Club, which I massively respect and I'm grateful for the past 3 years," he wrote on Thursday.

"I must however admit my mistake and apologise for my choice of words, will be more careful in the future.

"Wishing the club the best in the future."

I owe Villa the world but Man Utd are above them - Tielemans

Tielemans, who helped Belgium reach the quarter-finals of the World Cup this summer, signed for United in July until 2031.

Last season he suffered separate calf and ankle problems that restricted him to 35 appearances in all competitions for Villa, the lowest number in a campaign during his time in England.

He called his move to Old Trafford "the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football" and said signing for "such a special club" like United "feels incredible".

United take on AC Milan and Villa face Borussia Monchengladbach in their final pre-season games on Saturday, before the new Premier League campaign begins next weekend.

title: Super League confirm NRL investment offer
description: Super League confirm that they have received an investment offer from the Australian Rugby League Commission.
fullText:
Super League have confirmed that they have received an investment offer from the Australian Rugby League Commission.

Discussions have been ongoing between the two parties since last year.

In a brief statement, Rugby League commercial said Super League's 14 clubs had been informed of the offer on Thursday and that details "remain confidential".

Chairman of National Rugby League (NRL) Peter V'landys told BBC Sport last October that Super League was in danger of "a crash" if it did not find new ways to grow revenue.

In April, NRL chief executive Andrew Abdo said concerns that a deal between the sport's two leading competitions would lead to a talent drain from Super League were "completely unfounded".

"What we're trying to achieve is to make rugby league in the UK and Europe as strong as possible," he told BBC Sport.

"That's the exact opposite of it becoming a feeder pathway program."

Abdo also said that the NRL were looking for a partnership with Super League rather than a takeover of it.

At the time head of RL Commercial Rhodri Jones called the negotiations between Super League and the NRL "encouraging".

"The sport is open minded to investment," Jones told BBC Sport.

"The NRL is a natural fit. They are probably the front leaders in the negotiations that we are currently having with various parties."

When asked if the ARLC wanted to decide the make-up of an independent commission that would run Super League, Jones said: "That's their demand at this point in time.

"But at the moment, you could say that is a 'red line', because it's important that the UK game is represented. There is independence in our governance structure already."

Leeds Rhinos chairman Paul Caddick is among those to have raised concerns at the prospect of investment, previously saying, "we have no intention of being swallowed up".

The Super League began in 1996 when rugby league's premier European competition moved to being a summer competition.

Hull KR won the Grand Final last year to join St Helens, Wigan Warriors, Leeds Rhinos and Bradford Bulls as the only teams to have claimed the title.

title: Poland says it thwarted a Russian plot to kill an American citizen in Warsaw
description: A Russian plan to kill a Ukrainian American citizen in Warsaw was thwarted by Poland before it could be carried out, the Polish prime minister said Thursday, adding it was the first time that “someone...
fullText:
WARSAW (AP) — A Russian plan to kill a Ukrainian American citizen in Warsaw was thwarted by Poland before it could be carried out, the Polish prime minister said Thursday, adding it was the first time that "someone on the order of Russia" sought to attack a U.S. citizen on the territory of another NATO country.

Western officials have previously warned that Russia stepped up a campaign of targeted killings since President Vladimir Putin's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, saying they have disrupted several plots across Europe. But Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said this incident was unprecedented.

The suspect, who was allegedly recruited by Russia's secret services, was detained by Polish authorities on Aug. 7. He will be held in custody for three months, the Warsaw police said in a statement.

The American Ukrainian citizen "was uncomfortable for the Putin regime," Tusk said in a news conference, without elaborating.

The operation was carried out in cooperation with U.S. services, said Tomasz Siemoniak, Poland's minister overseeing intelligence services. He said the targeted victim was a U.S. citizen "of Ukrainian origin." Officials did not immediately provide further details.

The Russian Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The U.S. State Department said it was aware of the reports but said it had no additional information.

Russia has long been accused of targeting its enemies abroad, including by using rare poisons. But intelligence officials previously told The Associated Press that Russia's security services are now more brazen in their choice of targets, going after Russian activists and foreign supporters of Ukraine as well as military defectors.

"We must assume that the Putin regime will try to eliminate people who are inconvenient for various reasons, in various places around the world," Tusk said on Thursday. He said that Poland and others must be prepared to counter such actions.

Western officials see the campaign as connected to Russia's broader efforts to undermine European countries that support Ukraine. The AP has mapped about 200 acts of sabotage, arson and other disruption across Europe since the start of the war that officials have linked to Russia. President Vladimir Putin told the AP in June that Russia is not waging a sabotage campaign against Europe.

In 2006, British authorities accused Russia of being behind the killing of former FSB officer Alexander Litvinenko in London with radioactive polonium. The U.K. also blames Russia for the attempted killing of former Russian military intelligence officer Sergei Skripal in Salisbury in 2018 with the nerve agent Novichok.

German authorities said Russia organized the 2019 killing of Zelimkhan Khangoshvili, a former Chechen rebel commander who was shot in a Berlin park by Vadim Krasikov, a hitman who was later greeted by Putin after he was exchanged in a spy swap.

In June, a Russian artist who was critical of Putin was shot and killed at close range near his home in eastern Poland. Tusk said at the time that the killing of Robert Kuzovkov, known by the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, had the hallmarks of a political assassination. He suggested it was possible Russia was behind it but Polish officials have not yet attributed it to Moscow.

Last year French officials disrupted a plot which they believe was aimed at killing Vladimir Osechkin, a Russian exile who lives under police protection and works to help military defectors flee Putin's war. Lithuanian officials also disrupted a plot last year to kill a Lithuanian supporter of Ukraine and another against a Russian activist. Officials in Germany have similarly broken up two plots: one to target the head of a German weapons company supplying Ukraine, the other against a Ukrainian military official.

Polish authorities arrested a man in 2024 in what they said was a plot to assassinate Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. That year, a Russian helicopter pilot who defected was killed in Spain — with Russian operatives the prime suspects.

"This campaign is not by accident or chance," a senior European intelligence official previously told the AP. "There is political authorization."

Burrows reported from London. Stefanie Dazio in Berlin and Matthew Lee in Washington contributed to this report.

title: Henriques chasing 'cricket nirvana' with Portugal
description: Moises Henriques says helping Portugal qualify for their first-ever men's T20 World Cup would be cricket "nirvana" at the twilight of his playing career.
fullText:
Moises Henriques says helping Portugal qualify for their first-ever men's T20 World Cup would be cricket "nirvana" at the twilight of his playing career.

Henriques played four Tests, 16 one-day internationals and 24 T20s for Australia between 2009 and 2021.

The 39-year-old has switched allegiances to Portugal, the country of his birth, and will captain the team at a European sub-regional qualifying tournament in Finland starting on Friday.

Italy played at their maiden T20 World Cup earlier this year having started their campaign at the same level as Portugal.

Henriques said he "didn't even know Portugal had a cricket team" until five years ago but has been impressed by the quality of their squad.

"Obviously, the ideal, the nirvana, would be to replicate what Italy have done," Henriques told the BBC Stumped podcast.

"Whether that's realistic for this World Cup, or the following, I don't know. We'll only be able to tell in a couple games.

"I'm sure there's a lot of opposition that feel that they might be able to do something similar."

Henriques was born in Funchal on the island of Madeira but arrived in Australia aged two when his father Alvaro decided to up sticks and move the family to Sydney in search of a better life.

Alvaro, who played second division football in Portugal, took a job working in a warehouse, where he is still employed today.

Moises and his two younger brothers threw themselves into the Australian way of life, and that meant cricket.

"Moises isn't the most common name going around in an Australian school, especially at that time," Henriques explained.

"I had a few issues at school early on. I didn't speak English that well.

"Cricket gave me that little bit of confidence I probably needed as a kid to feel a part of something."

Stumped podcast: Should the ICC make the Cricket World Cup bigger?

Madeira's most famous son is Cristiano Ronaldo, and the island changed the name of its airport in honour of the Portuguese football star.

Henriques joked he "might get a helicopter pad" named after him, if he is able to skipper Portugal to the World Cup.

Portugal, ranked 37th in the world, will first have to come through the 10-team tournament in Finland, where they have drawn Czech Republic, Germany, Greece and Israel in Group B.

Should they progress, the next stage will be a European final regional qualifier with Scotland, Jersey and Denmark next year.

Henriques said while earning a Baggy Green will take some beating, the feeling of pulling on a Portugal shirt, and captaining the country, will be something special.

"I went back to Madeira last year and it was the first time I'd been back, but I felt really connected to the place," Henriques said.

"When I played for Australia, my family also felt I was representing them as well. I'm representing the motherland, so to speak, and it's going to feel somewhat similar.

"Hopefully we can make a positive impact trying to grow the sport in Portugal and probably Europe more broadly as well."

Henriques, who will also play for Glasgow Cosmic in the inaugural European T20 Premier League following the qualifier, is not the only player in Portugal's squad to have played professionally.

Batter Cameron Shekleton, 26, has played first-class cricket in South Africa and appeared for the Proteas A side.

Former New Zealand Under-19 captain Craig Cachopa, 34, represented Sussex, Auckland and Wellington.

"I was quietly and pleasantly surprised with the quality of cricketers that we've got in the team," Henriques said.

"There's a lot of high-level cricketers going around, which I probably wasn't expecting a few years ago when I first started entertaining the thought of playing."

One challenge that Henriques will face at the qualifier in Finland is playing on an artificial pitch for the first time in a few decades.

"It would be 25 years since I've actually played a game of cricket on a synthetic wicket," added the former Sydney Sixers skipper.

"I'm coming out of back surgery about five months ago so the biggest challenge bowling will be landing on a synthetic wicket on coming off a full run-up.

"Obviously we train a lot indoors on synthetic wickets so hopefully I can make the adjustment."

title: Handling hate and seeking stability - Fofana's Chelsea journey
description: Wesley Fofana shed tears, faced criticism for laughing at the wrong moment and exposed racist abuse last season but believes stability will lead to "amazing" Chelsea future.
fullText:
Wesley Fofana shed tears, faced criticism for laughing at the wrong moment and exposed racist abuse last season - but now he believes stability will lead to an "amazing" Chelsea future.

The 25-year-old centre-back has been a controversial figure because of the difficulties he has faced since his £75m move from Leicester City in 2022.

However, he is also a survivor. He is the last remaining signing from that summer and, following Marc Cucurella's move to Real Madrid, Chelsea's longest-serving player aside from academy graduate Reece James.

"Football is like this. It moves fast, but it is a good stat," said Fofana. "For me, some years were difficult, but now I'm back. I'm playing, I'm fit."

Fofana is right to be optimistic.

He is young, featured heavily under new manager Xabi Alonso in pre-season, and fit and healthy after injury troubles in recent seasons.

"Thanks, Filip," he jokes, referring to goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen punching him during an aerial challenge and denying him a truly injury-free campaign last season.

Still, Fofana says "small details" have helped him stay fit having broken his leg at Leicester before overcoming an ACL injury and hamstring surgery at Chelsea.

"For me, the most important thing last season was to be fit, just to remove this from my head - the injuries and other things," he explained.

Fofana reiterates it was his "dream" to join Chelsea, the club he supported as a boy growing up in Marseille, through his admiration for the Blues' former striker Didier Drogba.

However, Chelsea finished 10th in the Premier League last season and failed to win a trophy.

Fofana was arguably the fall guy for many supporters, not helped by footage of him laughing on the bench during a heavy Champions League defeat by Paris St-Germain in March.

He said it was not as significant as some made out and that those inside the club "know my mentality", but added: "When the team is not doing well, we need to find someone [to blame]. I can accept that.

"The club bought me for a very big transfer [fee]. I came with the ambition to be the best in my position and to help the team. So, when things go badly, I accept being the guy [people blame]."

The France defender could easily have pointed the finger at Chelsea themselves. Former manager Enzo Maresca left the club after a falling out with the hierarchy, while his replacement Liam Rosenior oversaw a five-game winless run without a goal and lost the support of large sections of the dressing room during his four-month spell.

"Of course we can use this as an excuse, but I think it's the players," said Fofana. "We didn't give everything. We lost some games, we produced some poor performances and we missed a lot of things.

"Of course you can't bring that into the new season, but I think everyone knows what was wrong last season. Everyone looked at themselves in the mirror."

There is a line that cannot be crossed.

Fofana, a Muslim whose father is from Ivory Coast, was racially abused on Instagram last season. He also highlighted abuse in March 2025.

He says it hurts to see those messages, but he will never stop calling it out.

"It is not a big thing to expose people who do that," he said. "For me, it is very important. For me and other players, we need to show what people are saying.

"We need to educate people. I think the people behind Instagram need to work on that. I exposed this on Instagram and Twitter [now called X] because I think they need to be more aware and more conscious of this problem.

"It is not only football. I think the world is a little bit like this and it is too easy to say some things. Sometimes I receive messages and I don't think these people are racist.

"They send monkey emojis because they are unhappy with the result and then, if I score in the next game, the same people support me.

"We need to educate people because it is not normal to talk like this. I understand that if I get a red card, you can be disappointed, but you cannot say these things."

Fofana says young players have shown him similar messages after matches and chosen not to do anything about them. Having received such abuse from a young age he is prepared to continue speaking out, even if it leads to criticism of his own character.

Mudryk's emotional return and 'leader' Palmer - inside Chelsea's pre-season

Alonso has picked his strongest XI for three of his five matches during pre-season, and all three featured Fofana.

However, Chelsea have signed Maxence Lacroix and have nine centre-backs on their books. In addition, the club also has a group of players it considers "untouchable", meaning they are not for sale - but Fofana does not feature on that list.

When this was put to Fofana, he replied: "Yes we have a lot, I think there are nine or 10. Everyone needs to be good, to train well and after the manager takes the decision. It's like this for everyone.

"Maybe some guys will leave, others will come again. For myself, it is about training well, trying to be fit and we will see what the manager does. If the club tells me they don't need me anymore, it is like this. Of course I will be sad but this is football. You can't say 'I have my place and I am sure to play'".

It seems unlikely Fofana will leave and, indeed, he wants to stay and believes in a positive future for Chelsea.

He is among the players who have been convinced by assurances from the sporting directors and board about a change of direction, embodied by the signings of senior players Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck.

Fofana says the duo, aged 36 and 35 respectively, "know how to win big games", will be "important in training sessions" and may give one or two players "a kicking" if they are slacking.

However, he believes managerial stability under Alonso will define whether Chelsea succeed or not.

"I think everyone knows we need stability," he adds. "We talked last season with the directors and they said the same thing. They think the same way as the players. We need stability."

title: Draper slumps to first-round loss in Cincinnati
description: Jack Draper slumps to a straight sets defeat in the first round of the Cincinnati Open after leading 5-2 in the second set.
fullText:
Jack Draper slumped to a straight sets defeat in the first round of the Cincinnati Open after leading 5-2 in the second set.

Playing in his first match since breaking down in tears during his return from injury last week, the Briton looked set to force a deciding set against Spain's Martin Landaluce.

But the former world number four spurned six set points as 20-year-old Landaluce won five straight games to clinch a 6-3 7-5 victory.

Draper, 24, finished with 47 unforced errors and 12 double faults against the world number 64.

He was playing just his second match since June having recently lost to Terence Atmane at the Canadian Open.

A persistent arm injury kept Draper sidelined and caused his world ranking to plummet from fourth to as low as 160th in a 12-month period.

Since injuring his shoulder at the US Open in August, Draper has struggled with bone bruising and pulled out of scheduled comebacks at Wimbledon and the Washington Open this summer.

While he did not appear to be injured against Landaluce, he tired during the second set and his confidence seemed gone once the Spaniard made it 5-5.

Draper has recently consulted biomechanics expert Carlos Cano in a bid to resolve his injury problems, with the 61-year-old Mexican having already helped Arthur Fery become British number one.

title: Rashford, Mainoo & transfers - Carrick calls for more signings
description: Before his first full season as Manchester United head coach, Michael Carrick explains why the club need more players, discusses why he is in a privileged position and talks Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo.
fullText:
Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is determined to keep pushing to improve his squad this summer.

Carrick is about to begin his first full Premier League campaign in charge at Old Trafford.

He is acutely aware of the responsibilities that come with being the public face of such a worldwide institution, which he says it is a "privilege" to lead.

However, it also means having to address thorny issues with the media, which currently include a perceived lack of signings.

Carrick says he is delighted with United's business so far – they have spent £83m to sign Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa, with the out-of-contract Karl Darlow also joining as back-up goalkeeper.

However, with weaknesses at left-back and in central midfield, as they prepare for a return to the Champions League after a two-year absence, Carrick knows the work cannot stop now.

Because in a summer where his club missed out on key targets such as Elliot Anderson and Matheus Fernandes because they refused to match rival offers and are spending less than newly promoted Ipswich and Coventry, Carrick knows more transfer business needs to be done despite a desire to avoid the costly mistakes of the past.

"We want more, we need more, we keep looking for how we can do that," he said.

"Money's money, I get that. We feel like we have to be pushing for everything we're involved in, while being realistic of what the recent history's looked like over a period of time.

"For now, we've got to make the most of it, but we've got to push every boundary we can to be able to win again, basically.

On a personal level, Carrick had an excellent day on Thursday as his daughter got the A-level grades she was hoping for.

He cut a relaxed figure, benefiting from a rare summer when his club have avoided draining trips further afield, instead travelling to Scandinavia for matches against Wrexham, Rosenborg, Atletico Madrid and Paris St-Germain, before facing Leeds in Dublin.

"I love the position I'm in," he said.

"There's the football side; the tactical, the training, putting the team together. Then there's the other side; being the face of it, leading it, trying to set the right messages, the right behaviours and right tone for what we want to look like as a football club.

"I never take anything that this position and this football club brings for granted."

Carrick was given a number of opportunities to say Marcus Rashford will still be a United player when the transfer window closes on 1 September, but didn't take them.

"He's our player," he kept repeating.

It was also noticeable that in talking about the England forward, he was keen to stress Rashford was not the only player in his squad he had previously coached, managed or been a team-mate of given it has been highlighted as an area of strength in the player's reintroduction.

"It is not a unique situation at all and [we] treat him exactly like any other player," he said.

However, many supporters have not forgiven Rashford for his coolness towards United during loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona, where everyone expected him to be this season.

It is accepted even by those who know him there is a world of difference between the disinterested figure he became under Ruben Amorim and the fully motivated one who is widely accepted to be the best player to come through the club's academy since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Ironically, Rashford's return to United colours is likely to be against Amorim's AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland, on Saturday.

Carrick feels the 28-year-old still has a lot to offer.

"Football's got different directions," he said. "You've got to manage through the states to have a career for 10 or 15 years. It's never going to be smooth sailing.

"But you've got to keep moving forward. If you keep looking back too much, it doesn't do anyone any favours.

"It's been good to have Marcus around this week. He's our player. He's a good player, and he gives us something a little bit different."

Rashford was not the only England player to return to the United fold on Sunday evening.

In a sense, it feels like back to square one for Carrick with the young midfielder.

When he took over from Amorim, after Darren Fletcher's two games in interim charge in January, he had to raise the confidence of a player of undoubted talent who had been virtually ignored by his boss.

At least Mainoo did come on as a substitute for Amorim in the Premier League last season. He didn't even do that for Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad, even though it seemed England were crying out for his ball retaining abilities in the latter stages of the competition.

Carrick knows how Mainoo feels. He was similarly overlooked by Fabio Capello during the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.

Carrick spoke to Mainoo "through the World Cup" and says he has been "in great spirits" this week.

"I spoke to him all the way through the World Cup, not loads, but little bits," he said.

"It's challenging. From the outside we all see the glitz, the glamour and all the positive sides of football.

"But players are human beings. We all have our ups and downs. It's important we support each other.

"It was a good experience for Kobbie. It's a World Cup and that is a big step.

"He's still such a young man and he's achieved so much, so quickly. To be at the stage he's at is an achievement."

title: LIV set to cancel season-ending Team Championship
description: LIV Golf players have been warned that the season-ending Team Championship later this month is set to be cancelled.
fullText:
LIV Golf players have been warned that the season-ending Team Championship later this month is set to be cancelled, BBC Sport has been told.

Tickets for the event in Michigan cannot now be purchased online, with LIV's official website stating both ground passes and hospitality passes are "no longer available".

As first reported by the Telegraph,, external next week's tournament in Indiana looks increasingly likely to be the final event in the 2026 campaign.

However, LIV Golf is yet to make an official announcement, amid further reports that Jon Rahm could soon leave the league.

In July, former world number one Martin Kaymer said he felt it was "highly likely" the Team Championship would be cancelled, although last week Cameron Smith said he still expected the event to proceed, and that players "would be disappointed if it wasn't".

Last week, the series said it had secured an unnamed lead investor to keep the competition running in 2027 after the withdrawal of Saudi Arabian financial backing.

The Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) said in April it would end its multibillion dollar bankrolling of the breakaway tour at the end of the season, plunging the future of the series into doubt.

LIV Golf secures unnamed lead investor for 2027

Tours form new alliance in latest blow to LIV Golf

Chief executive Scott O'Neil said a signed agreement with a new investor is in place and has been approved by the LIV Golf board, with the transaction expected to be completed in September. Until then, LIV bosses are said to be taking a disciplined approach to support its long-term sustainability and maintain operations.

No details of the amount of money that will be invested were announced. PIF has pumped in more than $5bn (£3.71bn) since the league launched in 2022.

O'Neil added LIV will make its players "majority equity holders" in the competition, calling it "a first for a major global sports league".

The LIV press release said the proposed deal with the lead investor is for "2027 and beyond".

The competition will reduce to 10 events from next season, with five in the United States and five held around the world.

There were 14 events planned for the 2026 season but in April, LIV postponed June's New Orleans competition amid questions over its future and has not announced a rescheduled date.

Last week, O'Neil said LIV was focused on "finishing the 2026 season strong", but made no explicit mention of the final two events scheduled this season, in Indianapolis from 23 August and the concluding Team Championship in Michigan from 30 August.

Alongside Rahm, major winners including Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith, Martin Kaymer and Sergio Garcia remain part of the LIV roster after having left the PGA Tour.

American major champions Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed rejoined the PGA Tour after it introduced a returning member programme.

Last week, when asked about the series' biggest stars, O'Neil said: "I think when you have a global game and you have 57 players from 21 countries and you're playing in 10 countries on five continents, how you define stars gets really interesting.

"So while I have all the time in the world for Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau, I think I'd be remiss in saying they're not only two of the biggest, best golfers on the planet, but I think they're some of the biggest stars in sports, let alone golf.

"Would certainly love them to come along for the ride and journey because they carry maybe more weight than anybody in the game and I have a lot of time for that."

In July, the PGA Tour and DP World Tour struck an alliance with the Asian Tour in another blow to LIV Golf.

LIV was founded in 2021 and launched the following year with 54-hole events, taking its name from the Roman numeral for 54.

However, it moved to the traditional 72-hole format for golf tournaments from this season.

title: Leicester City put up for sale for more than £200m
description: Leicester City's Thai owners King Power are hoping to sell the club after 16 years, for more than £200m.
fullText:
Leicester City are looking to sell the club for more than £200m, with its Thai owners King Power ready to leave after 16 years.

The Foxes have had an eight-page sales booklet produced by a leading US investment bank to help offload the one-time Premier League title winners.

Citigroup lists the Foxes, its women's team, and other major assets - including the 32,000-seat King Power Stadium and its Seagrave training facility which was opened in 2020 and is valued at £121m - as well as OH Leuven, Leicester's Belgian sister club, as up for sale in a brochure titled 'Project Lineup'.

The document, seen by BBC Sport, values the club's physical assets at more than £200m, though no specific sum has been attributed to the sale of its struggling teams.

The brochure speaks of "a rare opportunity to acquire a club with an excellent track record of winning promotions to higher divisions".

Leicester's successes, including the 5,000-1 Premier League title win of 2016 and the FA Cup triumph five years later, are well promoted in the brochure, while their place in League One, after back-to-back relegations from the top flight and the Championship, fail to get a mention.

The club's turnover, which Citigroup forecast to be more than £97m for the 2026 financial year are also part of the pitch, but the years of financial losses and the club's debts - which, as outlined in its 2025 accounts, include £103.6m in bank loans - are omitted.

In the years that the club yo-yoed between the Premier League and Championship, with two relegations from the top flight in three years between 2023 and 2025, the club lost more than £180m.

Listen to a special When You're Smiling podcast on BBC Radio Leicester at 18:00 BST

A secret invite and other 'pinch-me' moments before Leicester woke up

Martin makes winning start as Leicester go through

King Power, run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family, bought Leicester for £35m from Milan Mandaric in 2010.

Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha is currently chairman after his father Khun Vichai died in a helicopter crash outside the stadium in 2019.

Efforts to put the third-tier club up for sale were first reported in the Financial Times, external in July, but the product brochure now being circulated to prospective buyers is public confirmation that new investors are being sought.

The sale process comes just eight months on from Khun Top saying he is shouldering the blame for the club's drastic recent demise.

There have been growing calls from disgruntled fans for the club to be sold, with the most vocal showing coming outside King Power Stadium after relegation from the Championship was confirmed last season.

Leicester's struggles in recent years have come at a time when the King Power duty-free business in Thailand, which has been intrinsically linked to the club since the Srivaddhanaprabha family bought the Foxes, has also endured financial difficulties.

Despite the club's issues, Leicester City is being positioned for sale as one of only five clubs to have won all three major English trophies - the Premier League, the FA Cup and the League Cup - since 2000.

The document also outlines the potential of the club's academy, stating the Foxes have a "strong talent pipeline backed by leading scouting infrastructure, active transfer management and highly developed academy system consistently producing top players".

Leicester sold academy graduate Jeremy Monga to Manchester City for £10m last month.

Leicester, relegated to League One for just the second time in their history last season, will start their latest campaign in the third tier under head coach Russell Martin at Notts County on Saturday.

Leicester declined to comment on the sale brochure when contacted by BBC Sport.

Analysis from Owynn Palmer-Atkin, BBC Radio Leicester

For some time, a growing portion of Leicester City fans have been calling for King Power to sell the football club.

Now, it appears they have got the beginning of their wish.

Despite incredible, fairytale-like success; a decline such as the one seen at King Power Stadium over the last half a decade cannot go unnoticed.

King Power changed the aspirations, the expectations and the definition of success at Leicester City. Now, they have to be held up against those same standards.

There are clear physical assets, but with the club now in its lowest position since 2009, a huge amount of time, effort and cash will be required to get it back to the Premier League.

The question now is, who wants to buy Leicester City?

title: The main contenders to replace Rodri at Man City
description: As a move for Manchester City midfielder Rodri looks increasingly likely, BBC Sport takes a look at the options to replace him.
fullText:
Enzo Maresca has been in his new job as Manchester City boss just six weeks, but already he may be on the cusp of having to make a tough decision.

With Rodri heavily linked with a move back to his native Spain, Maresca's first challenge may well be to find a replacement for a World Cup-winning captain and Ballon d'Or winner.

Rodri, 30, is in the final year of his contract and City have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Barcelona following interest from Real Madrid.

After helping the Blues win the Treble in 2023 then triumphing at the Euros with Spain a year later, an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed Rodri's dominance somewhat.

But he showed glimpses of his brilliance for City last season before returning to the Rodri of old as he captained Spain to World Cup success in the summer.

His stock is high, and a move from Manchester after seven seasons with the club would leave a huge hole for Maresca to fill.

So who are the leading candidates to step into the Spaniard's boots?

Age: 18 Country: Morocco Club: Lille

Talk of City signing Bouaddi has been rumbling all summer, and the club have reportedly held talks with the Moroccan,, external who would cost an estimated £85m.

Bouaddi is said to be keen on the move.

The teenager impressed at this summer's World Cup after a starring role in Lille's Champions League victory over Real Madrid in 2024 announced him on the big stage.

Bouaddi functions as a deep-lying conductor - much in the same vein as Rodri - and would complement summer signing Elliot Anderson, who is more of a box-to-box midfielder.

Taking into account the loss of Bernardo Silva, it is not just Rodri that City are trying to replace and, with 30 Ligue 1 appearances last season, Bouaddi possesses a level of experience beyond his age.

Age: 25 Country: Argentina Club: Chelsea

City have been heavily linked with Fernandez, and he is currently the favoured option for Maresca, who worked with him at Chelsea.

But the London club are expected to stand firm on their £120m valuation - a hefty sum considering City have already spent £116m on Anderson.

Maresca made Fernandez captain at Chelsea in the absence of Reece James. The Italian clearly sees Fernandez as not only a talented player but also a leader, something City would be shorn of should Rodri move on.

No-one has made more Premier League appearances under Maresca than the Argentine, whose attacking intent and runs into the opposition box are attractive.

Fernandez returned to Chelsea training this week after helping Argentina reach the World Cup final, where he was sent off as they lost to Spain.

And Chelsea have set a deadline of 17:00 BST on Friday for any offers for him as they look to bring an end to uncertainty over his future before the season.

The club are said to be willing to fully reintegrate him into the squad and would continue to regard him as a key player.

Fernandez scored 15 goals and provided seven assists in 54 appearances for Chelsea last season. Of the options in this list, he also comes out on top for successful passes, passes into the box and successful passes into the final third.

Age: 22 Country: England Club: Bournemouth

City have explored a potential move for England international Scott this summer.

The 22-year-old has rejected contract offers from the Cherries amid interest from other Premier League teams, though his current deal does not expire until 2028 and the club have expressed their desire to keep him.

Bournemouth rejected a £64m bid from Chelsea for the midfielder last month and made it clear that any further approaches would not be welcomed. Advances from Arsenal have also been knocked back.

Scott's energy and ball-carrying ability suit Maresca's preferred style of play - with a heavy emphasis on possession - while his passes into the box and ability to win duels make him an appealing option.

Age: 27 Country: Argentina Club: Liverpool

Perhaps the most surprising name to be linked with City is Mac Allister, but the Blues have explored a potential move for him.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract at Anfield and has been a consistent presence in the Reds' midfield during his time there, though he struggled for form during a troublesome 2025-26 season.

As a Premier League winner, Mac Allister would bring top-flight experience and be a ready-made candidate to slot into City's midfield.

A versatile player, he can play as a holding midfielder or as a more box-to-box option. As the oldest option on this list, Mac Allister would also offer a wealth of experience.

Should Rodri depart, Maresca's side are somewhat lacking in leaders, with club captain Silva and experienced campaigners John Stones and Nathan Ake also leaving.

Maresca is believed to want a homegrown player in the leadership group, which consists of Rodri, Ruben Dias and Erling Haaland.

Despite his outspoken nature, Haaland does not seem suited to Maresca's demands of a captain on the pitch, which leaves Dias as the front-runner for the armband.

"Erling was one of the first to send a message when I joined the club," said Maresca.

"At Leicester and Chelsea I had a rule that when we scored the captain had to come to the bench, not to celebrate, but for instructions. But if he scores, then he can celebrate.

"If Erling is the captain, we have a problem... can you imagine?"

Phil Foden has captained City during pre-season and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma is a vocal presence on the pitch, while defender Marc Guehi skippered former club Crystal Palace.

Vultures are disappearing in Nigeria - but the 'Vulture King' is fighting to reverse the trend
description: Some see them as sinister or hunt them for ritual use but these birds play a vital role in nature's cycle.
fullText:
"People fear the environment where the shrine is. No evil will ever happen here. So, nobody fights vultures that perch here," a man they call the Vulture King tells the BBC.

Mostly associated with death and decay, perhaps it is not surprising that when vultures disappeared from the skies across many West African cities, they were not missed.

Yet across the continent, their disappearance is becoming impossible to ignore, as conservationists warn that hunting linked to traditional beliefs and spiritual practices continues to threaten several vulture species to the point of near extinction.

Without vultures, ecosystems would lose a natural defence against the spread of disease.

Thankfully in one part of south-eastern Nigeria, residents are bucking the trend.

Awka-Etiti is home to a sacred forest surrounding a shrine dedicated to a deity known as Nguma.

At first glance, the site is an unremarkable cluster of tall trees wrapped in thick greenery. But at its heart stands an ancient tree that locals say has watched over the community for hundreds of years, and remains the spiritual home of the shrine.

This is a largely Christian community but some residents continue to observe traditional practices, in which vultures play a key role.

Local resident Chukwuemeka Igwe, who has earned the nickname King of Vulture, thanks to his tireless volunteer work with Nigeria Conservation Foundation (NCF), says "the indigenous don't hunt vultures".

Instead, locals sometimes offer fresh animal sacrifices at the shrine which attract the birds, he explains.

"And there is an adage we use here that says: 'When you put down a sacrifice and you do not see vulture[s], know that something happened in the spirit world'."

It means that vultures are a good omen when a sacrifice has been made because their presence suggests that the deity has accepted the sacrifice and heard the residents' appeal to its power.

Now in his 50s, Igwe says the birds have been a feature of daily life in this town for as long as he can remember, walking around among humans and scavenging for food.

Yet for many who venture into the wild elsewhere on the continent, vultures are not the first birds to capture their attention. Rarely do we stop to admire vultures through binoculars or photograph in awe.

In the eyes of many people, vultures are downright ugly. But scientists say they provide one of nature's most important cleaning services.

Vultures consume dead animals within hours, helping prevent carcasses from becoming breeding grounds for dangerous bacteria and diseases.

Their disappearance can have serious consequences, says NCF conservation biologist Stella Egbe: "In places where the total collapse of vultures has happened, there has been impact of rising zoonotic diseases."

Vultures' powerful stomach acids allow them to safely consume infected animals, helping stop diseases such as anthrax and rabies from spreading.

Without vultures, experts warn ecosystems lose a natural defence system.

Rapid urban growth across Africa has also played its part, transforming landscapes, and destroying many of the tall trees that the birds nest in.

Habitat loss is far from the only factor.

Poisoning is the cause of death for an estimated 60% of vultures in Africa, according to BirdLife International.

These issues will be high on the agenda when researchers from across the region meet in Abuja later this year to review the West African Vulture Conservation Action Plan, which was drafted in 2022.

Experts say the use of vultures and their body parts in traditional medicine and Vodun (also known as Voodoo) has emerged as one of the most significant drivers of their decline, especially in West and southern Africa.

Dead adult vultures in Nigeria used to sell for around 25,000 to 30,000 naira ($18 to $22; £13 to £16) each - but can now fetch up to 200,000 naira ($145; £107) per bird, says Egbe.

Vulture eggs and nests are increasingly targeted too, which for such a slow-breeding species is a catastrophic and "shocking" development, says Egbe.

Adult vultures usually reach sexual maturity between the ages of five and seven, and produce only one chick every year or two. Plus many young vultures do not survive their first year.

"And so you imagine what will happen if a nest is removed and eggs are removed. That means a pair of vultures will not have a next generation for that year. So in addition to hunting, you're removing their habitat, you're removing their homes," she adds.

Seven species of vultures in Africa are now classified as globally Endangered or Critically Endangered by BirdLife International, the authority for birds on the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List.

A recent BirdLife report says African vulture populations have fallen by between 80% and 97% over a period of 50 years.

The group also says that in January 2020 more than 2,000 hooded vultures were found dead in Guinea-Bissau, many with their heads removed - a sign of belief-based practices rather than natural causes, researchers say.

As vulture populations continue to fall across the region, conservationists have been searching for communities where these birds are not hunted, feared or exploited.

They found one such example in Awka-Etiti.

Yet in recent years, Igwe says he and other residents became worried when they noticed outsiders arriving to hunt the birds and vulture numbers dwindled.

In his quest to save the birds he visits markets, buses and public spaces to spread the word: "I tell them that vulture is helpful to human life".

He says he "cannot run away" from his unusual nickname of Ezeudene, or the King of Vulture.

"I'm fighting to make nature exist the way it's supposed to be."

Working with the NCF for the past six years, Igwe has mobilised community leaders, local groups and security teams to protect the birds from outside hunters, with local bylaws now helping to formalise their protection.

Local volunteers monitoring the birds say they have now recorded more than 160 vultures, up from about 20 recorded in 2017.

Nigeria has become a major hub for the illegal trade of vultures, conservationists say, partly because of its biodiversity and porous borders.

"We are doing everything possible to make sure that the smuggling of items, including vultures, including donkeys, and other species outside the country is suppressed to the barest minimum," insists Abdullahi Maiwada, a spokesman for the Nigerian Customs Service.

He says customs officials have carried out seizures of protected wildlife and supported prosecutions linked to illegal trafficking.

It is an example of how Nigeria is trying to live up its commitments as a member of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (Cites) - under which endangered species are not allowed to be traded across borders.

But Maiwada admits to the BBC that enforcement alone is not enough - education will be crucial too.

"We may not be able to do it without the cooperation or understanding of members of the community," he continues. "If people understand why these species should be preserved, then our enforcement will only be complementary to those who decide to be recalcitrant."

That message has been at the heart of conservation work in Awka-Etiti and across parts of Nigeria.

Although reliable population data remains limited, conservationists say there are encouraging signs in Awka-Etiti, with local engagement helping residents become vigilant against outside hunters.

"The missing vultures are almost back. If you go to the marketplace now, you see vultures. At one time they disappeared, but now they are coming back," Igwe confirms.

Egbe believes that this small, south-eastern town demonstrates what is possible when communities lead conservation efforts.

"What we've done in Awka-Etiti is one very good example of a success story where people have taken charge of what's going on in their environment. That makes us happy."

For Igwe, every returning bird represents hope.

But with populations still collapsing across Africa, he knows protecting them will require much more than one community.

title: Wisconsin Democratic candidate for governor David Crowley reveals he won't campaign with Hasan Piker
description: David Crowley said he won't campaign with Hasan Piker, distancing himself from platforms he says divide the Democratic Party ahead of the Wisconsin governor's race.
fullText:
Democratic Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate David Crowley said he would not be campaigning with far-left socialist Twitch streamer Hasan Piker during an interview released on Wednesday.

Crowley said he didn't want to lend credibility to platforms that further divide the Democratic Party, in an interview with WISN 12 News.

"I don't want to lend credibility to platforms, if you will, that I believe further divide us as a community, further divide Democrats, or further divide this country. But, I do know that we have to focus on bringing everybody under this tent," Crowley said.

Meet The Democrat Who Narrowly Defeated Socialist Rival In Key Swing-state Battle Over The Party's Future

"So, I'm always willing to have those tough conversations. But we also have to utilize not just myself —there are many community members, there are many voters, there are many supporters that we can empower to bring people to be a part of this big tent we call the Democratic Party," he said.

WISN 12 News' Matt Smith asked Crowley directly if he was talking about Piker specifically, and if he was planning to campaign with the streamer.

"I'm talking about anybody who focuses on divisive language," he said, adding, "I don't plan on campaigning with Hasan, if that's what you're asking me. No."

Piker campaigned alongside Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist who ran against Crowley in the Wisconsin gubernatorial primary.

Hasan Piker Calls For Democrats Who Oppose Abdul El-sayed To Be 'Punished'

The streamer reacted to Crowley's remarks on X.

"this is devastating news for me, i however wish crowley the best of luck for the wisconsin trifecta. hope he takes some of the great policies that brought out 300k wisconsinites into consideration as the dems work to defeat tom tiffany as a unified front!" Piker wrote.

Piker said Wednesday that "the knives will be out" for the socialist left after Hong's loss in the Wisconsin primary.

Piker argued during his livestream that Democratic establishment figures will work harder to stop insurgent candidates because they no longer underestimate the progressive movement.

"It will be more difficult, though, because the establishment will not underestimate us. It will continue to undermine us, but they will not underestimate us," Piker said. "So, the knives will be out."

Eric Ham, a political analyst, told Fox News Digital in a statement that Crowley's comments "fuel division within the Democratic Party and only makes it harder for the party to be a viable check on the Trump administration.

"Moreover, as the economy falters and the war in Iran grows more unpopular, Democrats have a very real shot at tangible pickups, not just in Washington, but in state and local races. Wisconsin is a clear example of this. Now is the time for the party, left and center, to unify behind its candidates and chart clear messaging and contrasts versus Republicans. Otherwise, Democrats risk squandering tremendous gains in November," Ham continued.

The Democratic Socialists of America did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: Trump White House says it's losing $19B-$26B a year in revenue as countries dodge tariffs
description: The Trump White House said in a new report on Thursday that countries are routing their exports through third countries to avoid U.S. tariffs, estimating that there are tax revenue losses of $19 billi...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump White House said in a new report on Thursday that countries are routing their exports through third countries to avoid U.S. tariffs, estimating that there are tax revenue losses of $19 billion to $26 billion annually.

The report specifically highlights that China responded to new tariffs in 2018 by sending their goods to other nations ranging from Mexico to Malaysia for packaging and limited assembly — a practice known as transshipping. That pattern made it look like U.S. imports from China had dropped, but enabled Beijing to continue growing its manufacturing sector in ways that could challenge U.S. factories and employment.

Peter Navarro, the White House trade adviser, told reporters on a conference call that China is laundering its exports through more than 40 countries, though he claimed that the issues raised in the report were really more about other nations enabling the avoidance of tariffs.

"For years, the great transshipment scam has let communist China launder its exports," Navarro said.

The report comes ahead of a planned September visit by Chinese Leader Xi Jinping, who President Donald Trump described in flattering terms during his own visit to Beijing in May.

The Chinese government has described its relationship with the U.S. as one of "strategic stability," yet its government policies that support exports of manufactured goods have destabilized the auto, metals and electronics sectors in America, Europe, Japan and elsewhere.

Navarro said that other nations such as India could also transship to avoid new tariffs and said that new trade frameworks pursued by the Trump administration are going to contain provisions that ensure trade partners that engage in the practice will be penalized.

The Trump administration has levied high tariffs on much of the world in hopes of protecting U.S. manufacturers, hitting allies and rivals alike with import taxes. At the same time, those tariffs have created new inflationary pressures at home.

The report includes a range of estimates for the scale of transshipments to avoid tariffs, citing government and private sector numbers to estimate roughly $34.2 billion to $303 billion of goods transshipped each year. It used a central figure of $75 billion worth of goods being transshipped to estimate how much in tax revenues have been lost.

To address the challenge, Navarro said that U.S. Customs and Border Protection has started to use artificial intelligence in a prototype program to stop transshipments. Navarro said that when an importer has been found to have falsified the origins of a good, its imports can be retroactively tariffed going back roughly a year.

The president's tariffs during his second term have faced an array of legal challenges, with the Supreme Court overturning some of them in February. America continues to import more than it exports to the rest of the world, but the trade imbalance so far this year at $371 billion is running about $189 billion lower that it did during the same period last year.

title: Hegseth says reports about poor conditions aboard carrier are misrepresented
description: U.S.
fullText:
PANAMA CITY, Aug 13 (Reuters) - U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Thursday that reports about poor conditions aboard aircraft carrier the USS Abraham Lincoln ‌in the Middle East were "completely misrepresented."

Two military-focused outlets, Navy Times and Stars and ‌Stripes, reported suicide attempts and declining morale on the 5,000-person ship, which has been at sea since November 2025.

The ​carrier has been in the Middle East since January, supporting the U.S. war with Iran.

"We make sure every ship, every crew, every captain has everything we can provide them at every single moment. Some deployments are longer than others, and I have more respect and gratitude for those sailors ‌than anybody. What they do in ⁠those high seas in those austere conditions with less port calls — it's incredible," Hegseth told reporters during a visit to Panama.

Typically naval deployments are ⁠for between six and nine months, but during times of conflict, that can be extended.

Extended deployments can pose enormous strain on crews' mental health, particularly in wartime, and have always been a challenge ​for the ​U.S. Navy. Sailors must maintain a heightened state ​of alert and readiness, especially with ‌the threat of drone and missile attack from Iran.

A U.S. official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said the George Washington aircraft carrier is heading to the region with the intention of replacing the Lincoln carrier. That move was pre-planned, the official said.

Democratic lawmakers are unhappy about the extended deployment of the Lincoln carrier and the conditions on the ship.

"There have been widespread ‌reports of shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing ​issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns, and disruptions ​in the mail system, which have caused ​many care packages in route to the ship to be lost in ‌transit for months," U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal ​wrote to Hegseth and ​the Navy secretary this week.

When asked about reports of poor conditions on the Abraham Lincoln, White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said President Donald Trump and Hegseth were committed ​to ensuring the U.S. military was "equipped with ‌the resources necessary to counter any threat to the United States".
