title: May’s flowers wilted by bullpen in Brewers 4-3 loss
description: May’s stellar outing spoiled by bullpen and offense’s lack luster production
fullText:
West Coast nightmares continue to haunt the Brewers as the San Diego Padres finish the three-game series sweep in a 4-3 extra-inning affair. The Brewers are now 4-8 on the season when playing on the West Coast.

From Dustin May's stellar seven-inning performance to the four double plays turned by the defense, followed by a bullpen blowup and some other critical mistakes, today's game was filled with a lot of ups and downs. Things didn't get off on the right foot either in the bottom of the second as Joey Ortiz mishandled a groundball to allow Luis Rengifo to reach base safely. He did make it up a play later by turning the first of four double plays.

Entering today's ballgame, the Brewers had scored just four runs all series, which is a sight for sore eyes compared to what we've seen from this team all season. With the team avoiding some major injuries a night ago, the offense needed a spark, and that's what Gary Sánchez gave to them in the top of the second inning with a solo home run to left field.

There goes El Kraken 🐙 https://t.co/UesnAWKNdG pic.twitter.com/dJzJx6ejmv

Despite the rocky defensive play all series, and the rough start from Ortiz early in the first inning, the defense felt like it finally found its groove. During the bottom of the second inning, Jackson Merrill grounded into the Padres' second straight double play to quickly give his team two outs. Quickly resulting into another 1-2-3 inning as Austin Hays grounded out shortly thereafter.

Playing in his first game since August 8, Ortiz was trying to be another man in this lineup to provide another pop, but instead of using his bat, he walked with one out in the top of the third inning. After advancing to second base on a groundout, Brice Turang drove in Ortiz with a single to extend the Brewers' lead to 2-0.

May was stellar this afternoon in his second appearance in a Brewers uniform, throwing a quick and efficient seven innings of one-run ball on just four hits and two walks, while striking out six batters. His one blemish of the game came in the bottom of the third when Xander Bogaerts hit his 10th home run of the season to cut the Brewers' lead down to 2-1.

In terms of offense, both sides were quite stale going forward. In the bottom of the fourth inning, the bases were loaded for the Padres, with one out. In dire need to get out of the inning to maintain their lead, May forced Hays into an inning-ending double play, making it the third double play grounded into by the Padres in the game.

From that point on, the Padres offense was retired in order until the bottom of the eighth inning. Pat Murphy sent May back out to the mound for his eighth inning of work, as he had thrown less than 80 pitches at that point in the ballgame. A decision that felt like a no-brainer considering the four-game series with the Dodgers looming beginning tomorrow.

Dustin May: certified Brewer pic.twitter.com/mMQIuDiufx

May came out and walked Gavin Sheets on four straight balls to open up the bottom of the eighth. Chad Patrick then replaced May, and he then forced Bogaerts into a double play, clearing all but one from the bases. Then the command issues came for Patrick as he loaded the bases on back-to-back walks. Following the second walk, Aaron Ashby came in to take things over. Brewers killer Jake Cronenworth then singled to score Fernando Tatis Jr. to tie the game at 2-2.

Nothing happened on offense for the Brewers in the top of the ninth, but the Padres continued to be pesky, and more so, Merrill continued to be pesky, as he doubled with one out. After Luis Campusano popped out for the second out of the inning, Jase Bowen lined a ball into center field, where Garrett Mitchell stretched out to take away the win for the Padres, leaving the game at 2-2.

G LAYS OUT TO KEEP US TIED pic.twitter.com/1GJ1SFfJw8

After another quiet 10th inning from both offenses, the Brewers finally broke the silence in the top of the 11th inning. Once again, it was Sánchez who came through with the clutch hit as he doubled a ball off the third base bag to score Jihwan Bae, giving the Brewers a 3-2 lead. After a Mitchell walk with no outs, David Hamilton and Ortiz followed with strikeouts of their own to quickly put the Brewers down. Padres then walked Jackson Chourio before getting Turang to strike out to end the inning, wasting valuable time to extend the Brewers' lead.

El Gary delivers in the clutch pic.twitter.com/oVc2t8Mifo

Antonio Senzatela replaced closer Trevor Megill on the bump for the bottom of the 11th inning and was out to a great start by forcing a groundout. Then, Merrill drove in the tying run with a flyout to left field that should've been more if it wasn't for Luis Lara's spectacular catch. While trying to ride high on the catch, Campusano hit a single to drive in the winning run, securing the series sweep of the Brewers.

Looking back at this series, offense was the main issue, as it feels like almost everyone is in a slump. Today, though Sánchez carried the offense, he also hurt the defensive side of the ball with several passed balls and a play at the end of the game that resulted in poor positioning. Certainly not the way the Brewers want to be feeling heading into a four-game series with the Dodgers.

Despite getting two quality starts from Logan Henderson and May, the Brewers will look to get back on track tomorrow in Los Angeles with Shane Drohan on the mound. The offense will also look to generate more runs in this next series, as against the Padres they were 2-for-24 with runners in scoring position.

Tomorrow's game will be a late one as first pitch is scheduled for 9:10 p.m., and you can find that as normal on Brewers.TV and WTMJ 620.

title: WNBA denounces 'bad-faith efforts' in statement addressing Enes Kanter, Royce White draft declarations
description: Here's what the league's anti-hate task force had to say about two former NBA players 'declaring' for the WNBA Draft
fullText:
WNBA denounces 'bad-faith efforts' in statement addressing Enes Kanter, Royce White draft declarations originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

As the WNBA has been under the spotlight regarding a handful of controversies recently, league representatives met to discuss how to move forward.

The WNBA's anti-hate task force met on Wednesday amid the league facing questions about transgender athletes while its players have been subject to online vitriol. The league has always tried to promote inclusivity, but this season has had its fair share of questionable moments.

Therefore, it's important that the league makes sure everyone is on the same page entering the home stretch of the season. Here's what the league's anti-hate task force had to say.

MORE: What WNBA rulebook says about Enes Kanter Freedom's eligibility

The WNBA released a statement on Wednesday explaining that the league's anti-hate task force met and discussed recent events.

The discussions appeared to centre on both the eligibility of transgender athletes in the league and online vitriol directed toward players. The statement also denounced "bad-faith efforts" to use these topics against the league's efforts to promote inclusivity.

The WNBA’s anti-hate task force meet today.

USA TODAY received a statement from a league spokesperson about the meeting.

Full statement: pic.twitter.com/Tebn6gv9EH

MORE:Why Sophie Cunningham doubled down on transgender athlete stance

The WNBA has been at the center of a firestorm of controversy recently that has extended beyond on-court play. Most recently, former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White have put forth their efforts to enter the WNBA draft, arguing that the league's rules towards transgender athletes make them eligible to play.

Additionally, WNBA players are consistently facing online pushback towards their on-court play or off-court opinions from both passionate and casual fans. Therefore, the league felt the need to meet to discuss how to move forward.

MORE:What to know about WNBA transgender rallies, protests

In 2025, the WNBA announced the  No Space for Hate" as it aims to fight hate both on and off the court. That included creating a task force comprised of "league and team representatives" with support from the players association.

"As the WNBA continues to grow in popularity and influence, we're proud to launch 'No Space for Hate' — a league-wide initiative to better protect players, preserve the spirit of the game, and affirm the values of our league," commissioner Cathy Engelbert said last year. "We believe that basketball can be a unifying force — a place where people from all walks of life come together not just to watch a game, but to connect,"

The WNBA's Collective Bargaining Agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA," clearly stating that men are not eligible to play in the league. It doesn't have a specific article addressing the eligibility of transgender athletes, which is pretty standard among women's leagues in North America.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 6 of Cincinnati Bearcats training camp
description: Cincinnati Bearcats football training camp is into its second week. Here are five takeaways from UC beat reporter Scott Springer
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bearcats are into their second week of training camp and are coming up on three weeks away from the Nippert Stadium season opener against Boston College (Sept. 5).

Thus far, the offensive line has commanded the headlines with Preseason All-American guard Evan Tengesdahl recently making the "Freaks List" annually put out by Bruce Feldman of Fox Sports. On this Wednesday, Aug. 12, Tengesdahl added the Lombardi Watch List to his accolades.

The Lombardi Award is given to the nation's top college football lineman or linebacker who best exemplifies the character, discipline, grit, and leadership of Hall of Fame coach Vince Lombardi. Tengesdahl is one of 54 standouts selected nationwide and one of just six representatives from the Big 12.

"One of the most powerful players in college football."@EvanTengesdahl_ ➡️ 2026 @BruceFeldmanCFB Freaks List pic.twitter.com/Eq3oPGtnv7

The luxury of an indoor facility is not missing a beat in practice. In their new building, the Bearcats are just steps from their locker room to the field, while on dry days it's a short hike to Nippert Stadium.

Another reason to bypass Camp Higher Ground was also the size of the football staff. When then-coach Rick Minter started going to West Harrison, Indiana, there weren't as many coaches or support personnel. In a Power Four conference like the Big 12, there's more personnel and more effort needed to pull off a remote practice while using the same 2026 technology and sports science methods.

Most recently, the team required an additional hotel within driving distance to accommodate the extra staff. And if there was a thunderstorm, the only solution was to wait it out inside.

"This is the best I've been around facility-wise," fifth-year safety Jasper Beeler said. "The way we work here and the intensity, I haven't been able to do that at any other place. All that we have here is amazing."

Gradually, the August practices have gotten more physical. The chatter between defensive backs and receivers has been evident and the offense (white jerseys) and defense (black jerseys) have been pretty spirited this week.

Safety CJ Jones had a tremendous interception while battling for the ball with receiver Giyahni (Gio) Kontosis. Kontosis and JV Gibson have given some defensive backs fits, but Jones came away with the football.

Safety MJ Cannon also had a big goal-line play and things have been very competitive when there's a running play involved.

"I love it!" Beeler said. "It's football, man. At the end of the day, everybody wants to compete, everybody wants to win. Obviously, it's going to get physical; we're all grown men."

Beeler transferred to UC from Northern Illinois and is part of a group of safeties trying to fill the void of South Alabama transfer Ty Goodwill, who is out for the season with an Achilles injury. Goodwill sent his teammates a video shortly after getting out of surgery, asking about their progress.

At 6-foot-3 and 325 pounds, Tyo isn't afraid of much.

He raised and showed hogs as a kid and was a state meet wrestler and thrower (shot and discus) on the track team in addition to his punishing blocks. Now, he's enjoying the limelight with Tengesdahl and Joe Cotton as the "Pancake Trio", particularly when an offensive line coach a few years ago here didn't give him the time of day.

Tyo works out his frustrations on the field and likes to follow the ball after he's plowed the hole.

"I love getting down the field, blowing up piles, blowing up corners, safeties, whatever it is," Tyo said.

In the August 11 practice, it was Notre Dame transfer Gi'Bran Payne with the long touchdown run. Aug. 12, it was Zion Johnson with a few quick bursts. Johnson played late last year when Evan Pryor was sidelined and is the most experienced back in terms of being a Bearcat.

The UC backs range from 5-foot-8 to around 5-foot-10, and Johnson now has 192 pounds on his frame with good speed. Once he's through a hole, there's no turning back.

"I don't want to say nobody, but there's very few people catching me," Johnson said. "They (offensive line) are making the holes way, way bigger. They're just executing and doing their jobs. Today's practice was very physical, which was needed. From the offensive side, we just came out and wanted it."

Also getting in on the action Aug. 12 was Zylan Perry, who had a touchdown with some push from the offensive line and junior James Lewis and freshman Jayzon Thompson both had scores.

A former walk-on himself, Scott Satterfield has always enjoyed having key walk-ons. Antwan Peek Jr., came from Indian Hill as a walk-on defensive back and now is a scholarship key defender at outside linebacker. Edge rusher Drew Logan was put on scholarship last year.

At tight end, Lyviel Waters of Winton Woods has turned heads and found the end zone in the Aug. 12 practice with the entire offense running out to celebrate.

On the defensive line, Nathan Nunn is a 6-foot-2, 282-pound junior whose father is edge-rushers coach Robert Nunn. The elder Nunn has 19 years of NFL experience, including a Super Bowl win with the Giants. He's also coached NFL Hall of Famers Bruce Smith and Jason Taylor.

"One of the bright spots is Nunn," Satterfield said. "He's a guy that can play all over the D-line. He's a walk-on guy that's earned his stripes. He's going to give us some great minutes this year."

Said center Tyo, "Nunn's doing a great job. He's done a great job transforming his body and getting stronger."

Tyo also pointed out 6-foot-1, 320-pound freshman Jonathan Rulo from Belleville, Illinois, as someone to watch.

This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: 5 takeaways from Day 6 of Cincinnati Bearcats training camp

title: Could Chaz Coleman play again? Former Vols transfer sparks comeback speculation
description: Medically DQ'd top transfer DE Chaz Coleman showed himself training in a new social media post that has reignited questions about his football future.
fullText:
Could Chaz Coleman be making a return to the football field after being medically disqualified following a transfer to Tennessee this past offseason?

It appears it could be on the bingo card after a social media post he made Wednesday, Aug. 12.

College football's next big stars? 10 freshmen who could make instant impact in 2026

In that X post, Coleman showed four videos of himself going through drills at a gym. According to Adam Sparks of the Knoxville News Sentinel — part of the USA TODAY Network — the location is unknown, but the former Vols 6-4 defensive end is no longer with the football program or enrolled at Tennessee.

Coleman, ranked as the No. 3 edge rusher and No. 16 overall player in 247Sports' transfer rankings, was one of the Vols' top pickups in the portal this past offseason. He followed Penn State defensive coordinator Jim Knowles to Tennessee.

🙏🙏 pic.twitter.com/KAXjubPE0l

He was medically disqualified in late June by the Vols. As noted by Knox News, if a player is medically disqualified, he could transfer to another school and play in a future season if they are medically cleared. They are just no longer able to play at the school where they were medically disqualified.

"Real sorry not having Chaz. I hope the best for him as a young man," Knowles said of Coleman during a Aug. 4 media availability. "(Pass rush) is kind of how Chaz made his mark last year at Penn State. We just set up opportunities for him in the game to be creative and pass rush.

"So it's a question mark (for Tennessee's 2026 defense) and time will tell how that goes. But we need to have other tools in the toolbox to create the pass rush, if need be. And we'll have that."

Coleman finished with eight tackles, one broken-up pass, one sack and one forced fumble last season at Penn State.

Tennessee is set to open the season on Saturday, Sept. 5 against Furman at 3:30 p.m. ET at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tennessee.

title: Hamilton West Side tops Kentucky, reaches Little League World Series
description: The Hamilton West Side Little League baseball team has reached the Little League World Series for the first time since 2021.
fullText:
The Hamilton West Side Little League baseball team has reached the Little League World Series for the first time since 2021 after defeating Kentucky's North Oldham, 6-0, in Whitestown, Indiana, in the Great Lakes region championship game on ESPN2.

The 2026 Little League World Series begins on Wednesday, Aug. 19, in Williamsport, Pennsylvania. As the Great Lakes region winner, West Side will face the yet-to-be-determined Mountain Region champion on Aug. 20 at 2 p.m.

West Side starter Boone Treadway, the son of Badin head coach Brion Treadway, pitched a one-hit, complete-game shutout. He threw 62 pitches, and struck out nine.

"Feels amazing," Treadway told ESPN after the game. "I'm just glad to get to do it with this group of kids."

Josiah Infante hit a two-run homer during West Side's six-run first inning.

West Side is a 23-time Ohio state champion. In 2021, West Side advanced to the LLWS final before losing to Michigan.

West Side and North Oldham met twice in the Great Lakes regional. West Side won the first meeting, 11-4.

West Side cruised past Michigan and Indiana in the first two rounds of the tournament.

title: Kasey Kahne is as passionate and competitive as ever at Knoxville Nationals
description: He's back in the Knoxville Nationals and looks like a legitimate contender
fullText:
This is just what Kasey Kahne does.
Racers race.

Eight years removed from his last NASCAR Cup Series race, Kasey Kahne is 46-years-old and as busy as ever.

"It's been a really good year and it's been fun because I've done a lot of things away from the racetrack and at the racetrack this year and some unexpected things," Kahne told Motorsport.com on Wednesday before his Knoxville Nationals prelim night.

For example, Kahne finally earned his elusive first victory on the World of Outlaws tour back in May at Williams Grove Speedway. He did so, not behind the wheel of the Kasey Kahne Racing No. 4, but instead the No. 39M for the injured Anthony Macri.

He's back behind the wheel in his own car this week, alongside full-time driver and teammate Daison Pursley, who took over for the legendary Brad Sweet at the end of last season.

"Being in the Macri car, that was a completely unexpected phone call," Kahne said. "And then to get to run 10 races for that strong of a team and Anthony as a driver support just helped me a ton.

"So yeah, the racing stuff's been really fun this year. I have really enjoyed myself. And then there's pushing the No. 9 guys to keep improving. I haven't raced with them a ton this year, so this feels a little different, but it's been a really enjoyable season for sure."

Kahne continues to race, and continues to own cars at this level, all because he is still as competitive as he ever was. He wants to compete in every facet of this discipline possible.

"I never lost my passion for driving," Kahne said. "I've never lost the passion being competitive as an owner. Sure, I might not be good today but we have a chance to be really good tomorrow with Daison, and I am driven to figure out all of it.

"I still have that drive to be hands on. I'm passionate and competitive. So there's not a lot stopping me right now. Luckily, Amy (Long) and (kids) Ana and Tanner are supportive of me. If they weren't, then I wouldn't do it."

title: Aaron Rodgers wanted to play at Lambeau field one last time
description: Future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers played the vast majority of his games throughout his NFL career at Lambeau Field as a member of the Green Bay Packers. Now, as he enters the final season of his storied career, he’ll never have a chance to play there again, and it sounds like he’s a…
fullText:
Future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers played the vast majority of his games throughout his NFL career at Lambeau Field as a member of the Green Bay Packers. Now, as he enters the final season of his storied career, he'll never have a chance to play there again, and it sounds like he's a little sad about it.

During a recent interview, Rodgers lamented the fact that Thursday night's preseason game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Packers is not at Lambeau Field, which would have given him one last time to play at the stadium where he played his home games for 18 seasons.

During a Zoom call with Packers reporters on Wednesday, Rodgers admitted that he wishes the upcoming preseason game had been scheduled as a road contest rather than a home game, even though returning as a visiting player would have been "strange."

"100%, 100%," Rodgers said via ESPN. "When I heard it was possible to play both my former teams, I was really hoping this one was going to be in Green Bay, not just to get back at Lambeau one more time, but to head out to Chives [restaurant] for a dinner and maybe head out to Green Bay Country Club for a quick nine or something. I was really hoping it was going to be in Green Bay for a lot of reasons.

"It would have been strange, being in that [visitors] locker room and stuff, but I would have found my way over, like many former players have over the years … and see some of the guys and see some of the trainers and equipment staff and all the people I really care about that still work there. Yeah, I was definitely bummed out that we weren't in Lambeau for this one."

While Rodgers no longer plays for the Packers, his message for the team, the city, the organization, and the fans was clear.

Asked what he will miss the most when he is retired, Rodgers said: "Definitely the people I got to do it with." And that included Green Bay.

"That's what this game's all about," Rodgers added. "It's about the relationships, and I'm just most thankful for all the men and women, you know, who've been in my life through this game over the years. So many great people in Green Bay, in the entire organization, top to bottom. You know, just salt of the earth type of people. … But the thing that actually lasts the longest is those people that impact your life, and there's been a lot of those, a lot especially in Green Bay, it had a huge impact on my life. So I think about those people a lot."

title: Fact Check: FAKE Sports Journalist 'Marc Jacobs' Falsely Reported Russell Westbrook Was Signing With Hapoel Tel Aviv in Israel
description: Did a real sports journalist named "Marc Jacobs" report that Russell Westbrook was signing with Hapoel Tel Aviv in Israel? No, that's not true: There was no evidence that Westbrook, a 37-year-old NBA free agent, had signed with the Israeli...
fullText:
Did a real sports journalist named "Marc Jacobs" report that Russell Westbrook was signing with Hapoel Tel Aviv in Israel? No, that's not true: There was no evidence that Westbrook, a 37-year-old NBA free agent, had signed with the Israeli professional team as of Aug. 12, 2026. The claim came from a fake sports reporter on a parody account, citing a story that does not exist.

The claim appeared in a post and image (archived here) by the @MJacobsLF account on X on Aug. 9, 2026. It read:

REPORT: Russell #Westbrook and Hapoel Tel Aviv reportedly have mutual interest, with talks between the two sides continuing to expand. The former MVP is seriously considering a move overseas this season. Per @TheAthletic

A deal would mark the first time Westbrook plays professionally outside the NBA.

This is what the post looked like on X at the time of writing:

The Marc Jacobs X profile describes the persona as a "Senior NBA Writer & Reporter for @LakerFilm." Jacobs is not a mainstream, credentialed journalist and has fewer than 4,300 followers as of Aug. 12, 2026. The @LakerFilm account (archived here) had fewer than 40 followers as of Aug. 12, 2026, and had the display name "FOLLOW MJacobsLF."

Lead Stories searched Google News (archived here) and Yahoo News (archived here) and did not find any matching reports from credible news outlets reporting that Westbrook was in talks with Hapoel Tel Aviv. The searches used the terms "Russell Westbrook," "Hapoel Tel Aviv," and "Marc Jacobs."

However, several publications picked up the claim as legitimate reporting, including the Jerusalem Post (archived here), which later removed the story (archived here) from its website.

The post on X also falsely cited The Athletic (@TheAthletic) to substantiate its claim about Westbrook. The Athletic, owned by The New York Times Company, did not report the story (archived here). A Google Advanced Search of the site (archived here) by Lead Stories produced the same results.

Lead Stories ran the image of Westbrook in the post through Google Gemini (archived here), Google's AI assistant. The tool concluded that the image has a Google SynthID:

title: The NHL is considering another round of expansion. Is that a good thing?
description: The debate over continued NHL expansion is hot. Here’s what you need to know.
fullText:
The early days of NHL history can be divided into two 24-year blocks.

The first, from 1917 to 1941, featured a revolving door of teams with near-constant change. The second, 1942 to 1966, was more stable, with a group of six squads that remained in place.

The league doubled in size, bringing the total to 12. Additional squads would join one or two at a time over the next 33 years — some via expansion, others through the collapse of the World Hockey Association — and by the turn of the millennium, it was a 30-team league.

The additions of the Vegas Golden Knights in 2017 and the Seattle Kraken in 2021 brings the NHL to its current size: 32. But it doesn't seem to be stopping there.

Nothing is official yet, but the NHL is considering another round of expansion.

As always, the fans' opinions range from full support to total opposition. Both sides have valid reasons for their beliefs. Here are some points for fans to know as they form their own opinions.

A little bit of middle school math will tell you that 32 is divisible by a lot of different numbers.

It can be split evenly into two conferences of 16. Each conference can then be divided into two divisions of eight.

The new 84-game schedule makes it even better: In a given season, each team can play its divisional rivals four times, the remaining in-conference teams three times and the opposing conference squads twice.

Growing to 33 or 34 teams would make all that math uneven.

It wouldn't be the first time. The NHL has periodically had mismatched divisions throughout its history — as recent as 2020, just before the Kraken began playing.

But they just got it all solved. Why mess it up again?

As it stands now, 31 NHL fan bases watch their teams fail in a given year. There's only one Stanley Cup. Adding more teams means more disappointment.

If there were no repeat winners, each fan would get to see their team win two to three times in their life. There are plenty of repeat winners, though, making it likely that many fans will never watch their team hoist the trophy.

It's not only about winning, though.

Until 2017, more than half the teams in the league made the playoffs. Today, it's precisely half. If the playoff structure remains the same after expansion, it will be less than half.

Sports sell the fans on hope. If less than half the teams in the league get the hope of a playoff series, fans might lose interest quickly.

The solution would likely be a play-in series, similar to the NBA's system. NHL commissioner Gary Bettman is strongly opposed to that as it stands now, but perhaps he could be persuaded after additional expansion.

The league doubling in 1967 made it possible for players with no chance at an NHL career to become NHL regulars. There were twice as many roster spots available, after all.

Have you ever wondered why Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux were so dominant? They were obviously highly talented players, but much of their competition was equivalent to today's American Hockey League players. Connor McDavid and Nathan MacKinnon would have comparable stats if they had the same opportunity.

But adding an extra team or two wouldn't have the same effect — especially with the amount of NHL-caliber players without jobs.

Fans have joked on social media that you could comprise a playoff team out of the current unsigned free agents. A few of those guys still might land on teams before the season begins, but some will undoubtedly retire early or head to Europe.

If the talent is diluted a little bit, it won't be the worst thing, either. The league has occasionally changed its rules to allow more goals to be scored because it keeps fans engaged. The superstars having slightly weaker competition might accomplish that.

If possible, the league wants to put teams in Atlanta and either Houston or Austin. It is also reportedly considering going back to Arizona.

Can those areas really support hockey?

Bettman has proven time and time again that hockey can work in warm-weather locales. It was under his watch that Southern Florida, Anaheim, Dallas, Raleigh, Nashville and Las Vegas got teams. At the same time, he has seen teams fail in Atlanta and Phoenix.

The biggest draw for these particular cities is the population. In a metropolitan area of 7.8 million people, for example, there must be enough hockey fans to fill an 18,000-seat arena, right?

If Atlanta gets a team, it will be the NHL's third venture there. More favorable expansion draft rules might help the team be more competitive from the opening face-off. If it doesn't work, though, don't say they couldn't have seen it coming.

Fool me once? Shame on you. Fool me twice? Shame on you. Fool me three times? You know the rest.

A lot of American sports fans pay close attention to basketball, football and baseball. For whatever reason, though, hockey often gets overlooked.

The game is undeniably growing in the United States. People tend to latch onto hockey once it becomes accessible to them, so giving millions of extra people direct access to the sport's best league will naturally rope more people into the hockey family.

A common complaint among U.S.-based hockey fans is the insignificant coverage it gets from major sports networks — especially the ones that televise it. Getting more of the country's biggest TV markets hooked on hockey could increase the amount of attention the sport gets.

Adding, say, two more teams would mean 40 more people on any given night get to live out their dream of playing in the NHL. But the job creation reaches far beyond the players.

More people would need to be hired for coaching and front office roles; scouting positions; public relations specialists and content creators; equipment managers; athletic trainers and medical staff; business operations staff of every kind; reporters; ice maintenance crews; security and in-arena hospitality staff; vendors and more.

Thousands of extra people would get to work in professional sports — a dream that would otherwise be unachievable for many of them.

It would also have a significant impact on the local community.

Sports teams typically donate generously to charitable organizations. They invest heavily in local youth sports. They sponsor community events. Additionally, many businesses benefit economically from the team's existence.

As it currently stands, the Western Conference covers the bulk of North America's land mass. Many "Western" teams are much closer to the Atlantic Ocean than they are to the Pacific.

Take the Nashville Predators, for example. Of the five closest NHL teams to Nashville, three play in the Eastern Conference, while the Predators play in the West. This creates much more than the ideal amount of travel — especially when they meet teams from California in the playoffs.

They also play nine games this season in the Pacific time zone, with seven of them beginning at 9 p.m. Nashville time. It's difficult to get people to stay up to watch those games entirely.

The Chicago Blackhawks, St. Louis Blues, Minnesota Wild, Winnipeg Jets and Dallas Stars are all in the same boat.

Putting teams in Southern Texas and Atlanta wouldn't solve this problem, but bringing one back to Arizona would allow at least one of those teams to move to the Eastern Conference.

As the Deseret News wrote about in detail this summer, a rising salary cap isn't always best for the fans. Much of the reason it's rising is because it costs more to consume the game than ever before.

After all, the salary cap is calculated entirely from hockey-related revenue. When revenue goes up, so does the cap.

NHL expansion would increase both the supply and demand of tickets, merchandise and everything else that generates money for the league.

It would also decrease the likelihood of a future lockout. With an expansion fee of $2 billion per team divided among the 32 existing owners, as well as the steadily rising salary cap, neither the league nor the players have much financial reason to hold out.

title: Panthers reportedly reach agreement with Pro Bowl TE
description: The Panthers may be on the verge of adding some notable help to their TE room.
fullText:
The Carolina Panthers may be on the verge of adding some notable help at the tight end position.

According to ESPN senior NFL insider Adam Schefter, the Panthers have agreed to a one-year deal with tight end Darren Waller.

Waller entered the league as a sixth-round pick of the Baltimore Ravens back in 2015. But it wouldn't be until his time with the Oakland/Las Vegas Raiders that he'd emerge—breaking out for 90 receptions, 1,145 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 2019.

He'd follow that campaign up with a Pro Bowl campaign in 2020, where he tallied career-highs with 107 catches, 1,196 receiving yards and nine touchdowns.

After retiring ahead of the 2024 season, Waller returned to join the Miami Dolphins in 2025. He'd go on to amass 24 grabs for 283 yards and six touchdowns in nine games.

The 33-year-old Waller now joins a room headlined by Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans and Ja'Tavion Sanders—none of whom have recorded a season of at least 350 receiving yards over a combined eight years.

title: Galo beat Bragantino, take lead in Copa Sul-Americana
description: Atlético took the lead in the race for a place in the Copa Sudamericana quarterfinals. On Wednesday night (12), Galo beat Red Bull Bragantino 1-0 in Bragança Paulista in the first leg of the round o...
fullText:
Atlético took the lead in the race for a place in the Copa Sudamericana quarterfinals. On Wednesday night (12), Galo beat Red Bull Bragantino 1-0 in Bragança Paulista in the first leg of the round of 16, building an advantage for the return match at Arena MRV.

Once again playing away from Belo Horizonte, Atlético managed to leave the pitch with a win. The team repeated its strong away form and showed efficiency to get the result in a balanced match.

The Massa Atleticana also turned out in force in the interior of São Paulo. From start to finish, the fans backed Galo and created a great atmosphere in the stands, pushing the team for the full 90 minutes.

The first half was marked by balance. Both teams struggled to create clear chances and also made mistakes in passing and finishing.

Atlético's best chance came in the 19th minute. Victor Hugo received the ball and hit a low cross-shot, but goalkeeper Cleiton made the save. Bragantino responded near the end of the half, when Sasha got a shot away and forced Everson into action.

Still in the first half, Lyanco had to be replaced by Vitor Hugo, and the score remained goalless until the break.

In the second half, Atlético began to find more space, and Eduardo Domínguez made changes to the team. Cassierra, Igor Gomes, and Minda came on in place of Reinier, Victor Hugo, and Bermard.

Atlético managed to open the scoring in the 27th minute, when Igor Gomes won the ball back in midfield and found Cuello bursting forward at speed. The Argentine forward entered the box and challenged the opposing goalkeeper. The ball stayed alive after the first contact, and Cuello popped up again to finish and put Galo in front.

With the lead, Eduardo Domínguez brought on Cissé for Cuello, giving the team fresh energy in the closing stages.

Bragantino tried to press in search of an equalizer, but Atlético stayed organized defensively and managed to hold on to the advantage until the final whistle.

A 1-0 away win and an advantage secured for the decider.

Atlético will face Bragantino again next Wednesday (19) at 7:00 p.m. at Arena MRV. With the first-leg win, Galo only need a draw to secure qualification for the Copa Sudamericana quarterfinals.

title: Alec Burleson Knocks in 3 as Cardinals Overwhelm Phillies Wednesday
description: The St. Louis Cardinals were able to beat one of the National League’s best pitchers Wednesday as Alec Burleson’s 3 RBI’s helped the Cardinals beat the Phillies and win the series. Kyle Leahy was excellent again for the Cardinals as he threw 5 innings Wednesday allowing just 6 hits while striking out 6 and walking […]
fullText:
The St. Louis Cardinals were able to beat one of the National League's best pitchers Wednesday as Alec Burleson's 3 RBI's helped the Cardinals beat the Phillies and win the series.

Kyle Leahy was excellent again for the Cardinals as he threw 5 innings Wednesday allowing just 6 hits while striking out 6 and walking no one. He outpitched Zack Wheeler who also lasted 5 innings, but surrendered 6 hits while giving up 4 earned runs while striking out 5 and walking 1.

The St. Louis Cardinals were able to break through against Wheeler in the bottom of the 2nd inning when Jordan Walker hit a screaming single off an infielder's glove and then stole second. Nathan Church then sliced a 93 mph four-seam Wheeler fastball down the left field line for a double that scored Walker and gave the Cardinals an early 1-0 advantage.

The Phillies tied the game in the top of the 4th inning when Bryce Harper and Luis Arraez hit back-to-back doubles making it 1-1. The Cardinals would not just take back the lead in the bottom of the 5th inning, but break the game wide open after Prieto got his first hit of the year singling to lead off the inning. Two batters later, JJ Wetherholt singled advancing Prieto to third. Ivan Herrera singled in Prieto giving the Cardinals their lead back at 2-1. That would be followed by back-to-back doubles from Alec Burleson and Jordan Walker upping the Cardinals lead to 5-1 after 5 innings.

The Cardinals would add a couple runs in the bottom of the 7th inning thanks to another Alec Burleson RBI single and a Nathan Church sacrifice fly making it 7-1 Cardinals.

The St. Louis Cardinals bullpen did an excellent job holding the Phillies scoreless for the last half of the game. Justin Bruihl, Gordon Graceffo and Luis Gastelum threw a total of 4 scoreless innings locking up a series-winning victory for the Cardinals who now head to Chicago for another crucial series against the Chicago Cubs.

title: Steelers reuniting with former starting linebacker
description: Familiar with Patrick Graham’s defense, the Steelers’ newest player should fit right back in with Pittsburgh this fall.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are reuniting with a familiar face in their linebacker room.

Pittsburgh has reached agreement with free agent Elandon Roberts on a one-year contract, according to ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter.

Reunion: veteran linebacker Elandon Roberts, who played in Pittsburgh during the 2023-2024 seasons, reached agreement today with the Steelers on a one-year deal, per source. pic.twitter.com/Zpg0I72ghQ

Roberts played for the Steelers during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before joining the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025.

Roberts, 32, was a strong run defender at inside linebacker during his time in black and gold. He recorded 147 tackles, 15 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, two passes defended, and one forced fumble in 33 games in Pittsburgh (29 starts).

Roberts started all but one game for the Raiders last year and totaled 90 tackles and six tackles for loss, playing for now-Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham.

Roberts adds much-needed depth to the inside linebacker group, led by Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson.

The Steelers begin the preseason at Acrisure Stadium with a 7 p.m. kickoff Thursday against Green Bay.

title: Darren Waller agrees to terms with Panthers
description: A year after he ended his retirement to play for the Dolphins, veteran tight end Darren Waller is heading to Carolina.
fullText:
A year after he ended his retirement to play for the Dolphins, veteran tight end Darren Waller is heading to Carolina.

Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, Waller has agreed to terms on a one-year deal.

A sixth-round pick of the Ravens in 2015, Waller became a Pro Bowler with the Raiders in 2020.

Traded to the Giants in 2023, he retired after his first season in New York. He joined the Dolphins last year.

Waller, 33, has a pair of 1,100-yard seasons, both with the Raiders. In 2025, he caught 24 passes for 283 yards and six touchdowns in nine games with the Dolphins.

The Panthers currently have five tight ends on the roster: Tommy Tremble, Ja'Tavion Sanders, Caden Prieskorn, James Mitchell, and Feleipe Franks.

Panthers associate head coach and offensive specialist Darrell Bevell worked with Waller last year in Miami, where Bevell served as the quarterbacks coach and passing game coordinator.

title: Double murderer and rapist told to 'rot in prison' by relatives of victims and survivor
description: Simon Levy is jailed for life after murdering two women and raping another.
fullText:
Relatives of victims and a survivor of double murderer and serial sex offender Simon Levy have branded him a "parasite" who deserves to die behind bars.

Levy, 49, was jailed for life on Wednesday after murdering two women and raping another, all while he was on bail for a series of other sex assaults.

On Wednesday families of the two women he murdered faced him in court, as a survivor of one the attacks told him he was "not worthy" of any more of her "words or time".

The sister of murdered mother-of-four Sheryl Wilkins was in tears as she remembered a "beautiful soul who you cruelly took away in an evil act of crime".

Lindsey Hicks told the Old Bailey hearing: "There will never be enough words to express how I feel since losing my big sister Sheryl.

"You, Simon Levy, have destroyed our lives and we will never get over this."

"We should have been growing old together like sisters do and be there to support each other. Instead, I'm having to realise that one day in the near future I will be older than my big sister.

"We hope you spend the rest of your miserable life behind bars and we get justice for Sheryl. This last year has been the worst year of our lives; the pain you have put us through has been unbearable. Sheryl's life was taken unlawfully and violently."

Addressing Levy directly, as he sat wearing sunglasses for an eye condition in the dock, she added: "Know this, you lose. We get to leave here today knowing we will keep Sheryl alive by sharing memories about her and living for her.

"We will continue to live as a loving family through our loss, supporting each other. You don't get to take that away. I hope you rot in prison for the rest of your life."

Sheryl's mother Mary Wilkins said she believed her daughter's murder in August 2025 had meant Levy was finally brought to justice, saving the lives of other potential victims.

In a statement read by junior prosecutor Kerry Broome, she added: "Our Sheryl has ended your chances of hurting anyone else, she lost her life to do this but we truly believe Sheryl has saved countless women.

"You took away our beautiful daughter Sheryl. She was a mother, a sister, a daughter, a friend and a beloved family member. She had four beautiful children.

"Sheryl was taken from us one day before her 40th birthday, she had so many hopes and dreams. She should've celebrated her 40th birthday, she should've grown old with us, instead all of that was taken away."

"Sheryl's children had been robbed not only of their mother but their future with her. This was the destruction of a life, a family and a future.

"Sheryl's life mattered, Simon you have changed our lives forever but you cannot take away our love for Sheryl.

"We will continue to talk about her, we will continue to remember her."

Levy killed grandmother Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, in March 2025. Her daughter Nazly Johana Fuenmayor Valencia said in court her mother had come to the UK to give her family a better life.

"There's an emptiness that can't be filled. I have been ripped apart… we will never be the same again," she said,

"She was a truly special person who gave so much love to others. Her kindness, her smile and the love she shared so freely will stay with us forever.

"We have been living a nightmare we cannot wake up from. We don't know why she was taken from us. The rest of our lives will never be the same.

"My mum came to this country to give her children a better life and for safety. Instead her life was taken so cruelly."

A woman who survived Levy after he raped her in January 2025 said she could not forget his smell as he attacked her.

In a statement read by a prosecutor she said: "He took away my soul that night and he took away my dignity. He took my soul like a parasite.

"I feel like people have taken advantage of me all my life. I can't forget the smell of his sweaty hands on my mouth. I thought I would die.

"It's taken me a long time to trust people, I can trust a small number of friends.

"I want to try to forget this monster. This man is a parasite not worthy of any more of my words or time."

Police failings revealed as sex offender left free to murder and attack women

He had done the same to Wilkins before she was found behind a car park wall near Tottenham High Road, north London.

His rape attack had happened in the same car park, but despite the victim telling police where he lived he was not interviewed until after his two murders.

His case has posed serious questions for the authorities over why he was repeatedly set free on bail - despite increasing attacks on women.

Judge Mark Lucraft KC, the Recorder of London, sentenced Levy to a whole life prison term.

He told him: "You are clearly someone who ruthlessly exploits others for your own personal sexual satisfaction.

title: Five Hacks Every Garmin Cirqa User Should Know
description: Skip the $59.99 official arm band with a cheap DIY workaround.
fullText:
For Garmin fans who want 24/7 data, but don't want to wear their heavy-duty sports watch 24/7, the Garmin Cirqa ($199) is an exciting new alternative to Whoop, Fitbit Air, and other screenless smart bands. This is the company’s first screen-free smart band, built to track fitness and wellness features around the clock, without needing a subscription.

Because the Cirqa has no screen, you might default to only do what Garmin's automatic detection decides for it. But when it comes to making the most of the Cirqa from the moment you unbox, there are clever hacks worth knowing. Here are five tips of my favorites—some official, and some discovered by reviewers and the community in these early weeks since the device's launch.

This is one of the more underrated features on paper. In Garmin Connect, go to Garmin Devices > Health & Wellness > Broadcast Heart Rate, and turn on Device Control. Once that's enabled, you can hold the side button on the Cirqa itself for three seconds until the LED flashes yellow, and it'll start broadcasting your heart rate without needing to touch the app again.

The Cirqa can broadcast over ANT+ to essentially unlimited receiving devices at once, and simultaneously over Bluetooth Smart to up to three separate connections, which means you could realistically stream your live heart rate to a cycling computer, a gym treadmill display, and an app like Zwift all at the same time. For anyone who already owns a Cirqa and was about to buy a separate chest strap for gym equipment or a smart trainer setup, this alone can save the extra purchase.

The Cirqa has no display, so there's no obvious way to "check the time" on it. But if you like the feel of a ticking analog reminder, you can get close. In the Garmin Connect app, go to your device, then Notifications & Alerts, and look at the alert options tied to activity and movement. Turning on Move Alert (Garmin's inactivity reminder) gives you a light buzz once an hour during your active hours, functioning like an unofficial hourly chime (even though it's technically triggered by extended sitting rather than the clock itself). It won't be perfectly precise to the top of the hour every time, but in daily use it lands close enough, especially if you're someone who deliberately avoids glancing at a phone all day.

The same Notifications & Alerts menu is where the real wellness tracking happens. You can enable alerts for stress spikes, sleep score readiness, goal completion, and general movement, effectively turning the Cirqa into a mini coach for hydration breaks, stretch breaks, or a moment of mindfulness—all depending on how you choose to interpret the buzz.

For actual wake-ups, go to Alarms > Add Alarm in the app, set your time, and toggle on Smart Wake Alarm if you want it to try waking you during a lighter sleep stage within the 30 minutes before your set time, or Quiet Start if you'd rather it ramp up gradually instead of buzzing at full strength immediately. Worth knowing upfront: In my testing (and I'm not alone here), the Smart Wake Alarm has a reputation for being less "smart" than advertised. While I've never personally experienced it going off outside its intended window, all the "smart" alarm has ever done for me is worked like a plain fixed alarm regardless of your alleged sleep stage.

Since there's no screen, most people assume the only way to check the battery is to open Garmin Connect. There's actually a faster method built into the hardware itself, as long as you go in and set it up.

In the Garmin Connect app, go to your device settings and open Power Manager, then turn on the Battery Status option. Once that's enabled, double-tapping the physical sensor module triggers a single confirmation buzz, followed by the LED flashing a color that corresponds to your remaining charge:

Flashing green = Charging in process

Solid red = Critically low battery

Combined with the favorite activity and hold-for-broadcast button shortcuts, this reinforces the sense that the Cirqa's single button and LED light help set this smart band apart.

And on the activity side, remember to use the side button as your manual override for anything the automatic detection struggles with—which is a lot so far. And since the Cirqa has no built-in GPS chip, any distance, pace, or route data during an activity comes from your paired phone running the Garmin Connect app, so keep your phone nearby if you want a real map of your run or ride, not just heart rate and duration.

Garmin sells an upper-arm band separately for $59.99, so if you'd rather track from your bicep than your wrist, that's an option worth exploring—especially if you do activities where a wrist-worn band gets in the way. Plus, upper arm placement might improve your heart rate accuracy overall, since it gives the sensor better contact with a meatier part of the body with less wrist-movement noise.

If you want the upper-arm placement, but don't want to pay for Garmin's official accessory band, it might look like you have no options. The Cirqa pod uses narrow, non-standard 14mm spring pins, so it seems like it won't just clip into generic 20mm bands off the shelf.

A few users have shared this type of hack, and I think this video from @ChaseTheSummit explains it best. The workaround is to buy a small 14mm-to-20mm metal adapter (originally made for Casio G-Shock watches), available for $14.99 on Amazon. That adapter bridges the Cirqa's small pod to the much wider world of inexpensive, stretchy 20mm bicep bands. It's not going to match the fit or finish of Garmin's own accessory, but it's a clever money-saving option.

If you do try this DIY option, make sure you don't just yank the stock fabric band off the pod: Use a small pin pusher tool to compress the internal spring pins inward first, then remove it. Forcing it off without releasing the pins is a good way to damage the housing.

title: Everything Already Announced Ahead of Made by Google 2026
description: Google spilled the beans before its main event even kicked off.
fullText:
Made by Google 2026 officially starts at 6 p.m. ET on Wednesday, but you wouldn't know it from today's tech headlines. Some eight hours before the event was scheduled to begin, Google seemingly announced all of the new hardware and software features it plans to reveal during its main keynote. Unless the company is saving some secrets for the show, it appears all the actual news from Made by Google is already out there.

As such, we already know all about Google's new Pixel 11 lineup, including the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL. We've seen the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, the Pixel Watch 5, and even the Pixel Tag, Google's first AirTag competitor. Plus, Google shared some details on new features coming to these devices, as well as existing Pixel products. While we still need to wait until this evening to actually watch the full event, here's everything the company announced ahead of Made by Google 2026.

At first glance, Google's Pixel 11 series doesn't look all that different from the Pixel 10 series. The company chose to carry over the Pixel's current design, which means the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL all feature a large, oval camera bump on the back, and a small circular camera cutout on the front. However, Google says it reduced the Pixel 11's camera bar thickness by 40%, which it advertises makes for a "virtually bumpless" experience when using a "Made by Google" case.

The Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL are brighter this year: Google says the displays can reach up to 3,600 nits, with an upgraded anti-scratch coating that the company claims more than doubles scratch resistance compared to the Pixel 10 Pro. All things considered, Google says the 11 Pros are the most durable Pixels yet.

It turns out the storage rumors were true: Google is dropping the 128GB models this year. All three Pixel 11 phones start with 256GB of storage, which is great for keeping large files on-device, but not so great for your wallet. While the 256GB option costs as much as last year's 256GB Pixel 10 devices, Google effectively raised the cost of entry by eliminating the cheaper 128GB option. Now, the cheapest Pixel 11 starts at $899.

All three Pixel 11 devices come with the new Tensor G6 chip, which unsurprisingly brings upgrades over last year's Tensor G5. Google says this chip's CPU supports 25% faster web browsing and opens apps 15% quicker. The TPU handles 50% more compute, which means the G6 can process on-device AI functions 3.5 times faster than before, at 3.5 times the energy efficiency.

Perhaps Google's "funnest" feature this year is "HiLight," a new LED that lives in the camera bar. Google says you can rely on the light for alerts, so you can keep tabs on important updates while your phone is face down. For example, you can assign colors to different contacts, so you know who's calling without having to pick up your phone. Plus, the light can glow in specific patterns when you talk to Gemini to indicate whether the AI is listening, "thinking," or responding to you. However, as Marques Brownlee highlights, there isn't much else you can do with HiLight, which seems like a missed opportunity—especially when other Android manufacturers, like Nothing, offer a ton of customization with their LEDs. Google says it plans to add new capabilities in the future, like message notifications from favorite contacts, but we'll have to wait to see whether the company decides to take full advantage of this fun hardware feature.

Google's Pixel line has always been known for its cameras, and this year is likely no exception. Google says all three of its Pixel 11 phones come with major camera upgrades. The Pixel 11, for instance, has a 48MP main sensor that adds 56% more light sensitivity, and the 5x telephoto lens now supports 30x "Super Zoom," thanks to the Tensor G6 chip. The Pros get some unique updates of their own: Google says the main sensor on each is brand new this year, and the telephoto sensor is now bumped up to 48MP with 30% more light sensitivity. Portrait Mode now works at 5x, and "Pro Zoom" now works up to 120x. Google says the Pixel 11's low-light photography should also look better now, as Night Sight works 4.5 times faster.

The Pixel 11 comes in four colors: "Pistachio," "Hibiscus," "Frost," and "Obsidian." The Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL are available in "Canyon," "Fog," "Olive," and all-matte "Obsidian." They also come with faster charging, especially on the Pros. Those phones support Qi 2.2 charging at 25W, and you can get 15 hours of battery on the Pixel 11 Pro XL with just 15 minutes of wired charging—assuming you have the right setup.

Google also announced the successor to the Pixel 10 Pro Fold today, but like the Pixel 11 series, it's a bit of a "blink and you'll miss it" update. These phones are quite similar, though Google touts some slight design upgrades: The new foldable is nearly 10% lighter and 1mm thinner than before. It has the same IP68 water and dust resistance as before, but now, the new glass fiber composite materials make the Pixel 11 Pro Fold "nearly impossible to crack," or so says Google. The company claims the foldable is three times more durable than the previous iteration, with improved crease performance on the hinge.

Like the Pixel 11 series, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold's displays are brighter this year, also reaching 3,600 nits of peak brightness. The Fold also gets the HiLight LED, though nothing is different on the foldable's light. This phone also supports Qi2.2 at 25W, and you can get up to 50% charge in 30 minutes when using a 30W wired charger. Google says the foldable can reach up to 24 hours of battery life, so, theoretically, you should be able to make it through a full day without needing to top off.

The Fold also gets Google's newest Tensor G6 chip, this time with 16GB of RAM. Google says that powers its new "sign-to-text" feature, which it developed with the Deaf community. This feature lets you sign in Live Transcribe, which then translates your sign language into text. Google says the feature works with both one-handed and two-handed signing. This new Fold also gets a new 48MP main sensor, and the telephoto camera now supports up to 30x Super Zoom.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold comes in either Obsidian or Olive. The phone starts at $1,899.

Google also announced the fifth generation of its Pixel Watch line. The new watch comes with the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 Accelerated processor, with 50% more RAM and a 12% faster CPU than last year's Pixel Watch 4. Google says the Pixel Watch 5 is its most accurate GPS route tracking ever, with double the accuracy of previous models. The company claims its tracking accuracy beats the Apple Watch Ultra 3 and the Garmin Fenix 8 Pro.

Google says the Pixel Watch 5 has 15% more accurate sleep stage detection than before, so your sleep tracking should be 

While not specific to Pixel Watch 5, Google also announced "Health Guardian," a suite of features that track changes in your health over time, including trends in insulin resistance, blood pressure, sleep breathing quality, and the aforementioned breathing emergency detection. You'll get a monthly summary in the Google Health app that points out any notable changes. This works with "qualified Pixel Watches" and Fitbit Air, though Google didn't note exactly which Pixel Watches work with these new features.

The Pixel Watch 5 has a 3,000-nit "domed" Actua 360 display with 11 new complication styles. Google also added two new watch faces, with additional generative watch face options. The watch can run for up to 30 hours off the charger (41mm) or 40 hours (45mm).

It comes in Fog, Olive, or Canyon (41mm only), and starts at $399 (41mm) and $429 (45mm). There's also a Stephen Curry Special Edition (45mm) that starts at $579.

As it turns out, the rumors were also right about the Pixel Tag: Yes, Google has been working on its own version of Apple's AirTag. Instead of working with Apple's Find My network, Pixel Tag uses Google's Find Hub network to achieve the same goals. Pixel Tag can connect to more than a billion Android devices across the world to update its location using end-to-end encrypted information.

Google says the Pixel Tag is IP67 water- and dust-resistant, with a built-in speaker for locating the device. It also has its own button you can press to ping your phone, something AirTags don't come with. Like AirTags, Pixel Tags last one year on a single battery, which you can replace yourself.

Setting up a Pixel Tag is identical to setting up an AirTag: You hold the device near your phone, and setup instructions appear on-screen. From there, you can choose to share a Pixel Tag with up to 10 people. When you need to find a Pixel Tag, you can use both Ultra-Wideband and Bluetooth Channel Sounding for precision finding, which provides turn-by-turn directions to locate your tracker.

You can use Left Behind alerts to know whether you forgot an item, and your phone will tell you whether an unknown Pixel Tag is following you. Like AirTags, you can pick up a Pixel Tag for $29 a pop, or $99 for a four-pack. The Pixel Tag launches Nov. 11.

While Google isn't releasing any new earbuds today, it is updating its existing models. Pixel Buds Pro 2 are getting Dynamic ANC, which adjusts noise cancellation when the buds shift in your ears. You will be able to ask Gemini to adjust audio controls, such as setting bass levels, and Pixel Watch will be able to pause your earbuds' audio when it detects you fall asleep. Live Translate will work in over 70 languages when tapping your Buds, and Pixel Buds Pro 2 now come in Olive. (The software features start rolling out in September.)

Finally, Google announced new apps that, over the coming weeks, will connect to Gemini for additional functionality. That includes the following:

title: Here's How the Cameras on Google's New Pixel 11 Phones Compare to the iPhone
description: Google just dropped the specs on the new Pixel 11 cameras.
fullText:
Ahead of its annual Made by Google event in New York City, Google revealed the details of its upcoming line of Pixel 11 phones, including specs of their all-important cameras. Pixel 11 phones will come in three versions: the base Pixel 11, the Pixel 11 Pro, and the Pixel 11 Pro XL. The Pro and Pro XL cameras have the same features, while the base model sports a slightly scaled-down photographic system.

The standard Pixel 11's camera setup is a step up from the Pixel 10, but not a gigantic leap. The main improvement is the brighter main sensor; the lenses are close to last year's hardware. Here's how it breaks down:

Main: 48MP wide camera (rear) with a 1/1.56" sensor (larger than last year's model) to improve light input.

Ultrawide: 13MP, which is identical to the Pixel 10's ultrawide camera specs.

Telephoto: 10.8MP telephoto with 5X optical zoom and a 30x digital zoom. Also the same as the Pixel 10.

Front camera: 10.5MP, also identical to the Pixel 10.

Google is throwing the heavy hardware improvements into its pro-level phones, bumping up both the resolution and sensor sizes across almost every lens.

Main: 50MP wide camera, with a 1/1.3" sensor for improved light-gathering.

Ultrawide: 48MP ultrawide camera, a big leap from the 13MP ultrawide of the base model.

Telephoto: 48MP telephoto with 5X optical zoom and an "AI-powered" 120x Pro Zoom.

Front camera: The Pro's 42MP selfie camera is a big step up from the 10.5MP camera on the base Pixel 11.

With Apple's iPhones holding down over 50% of the U.S. smart phone market compared to Pixel's 3%, Google faces a real battle to win over buyers. Camera quality is a powerful weapon in its arsenal. Most consumers consider the camera an important choice when choosing between cell phones, and it's the most important feature for about half of younger users. Here's how Pixel 11's pro tier camera stacks up against the iPhone 17 Pro's best camera offerings.

Main sensor: The Pixel 11 Pro edges out Apple slightly with a 50MP lens compared to the iPhone 17 Pro's 48MP, but megapixels are more complex than just "more is better." Apple's main sensor is 1/1.28," which is slightly larger than the Pixel's 1/1.3" sensor, and sensor size is more important to low-light performance and dynamic range than raw pixels. So this one's closer to a wash than the megapixel numbers suggest.

Ultrawide: It's dead even. Both phones feature 48-megapixel ultrawide lenses.

Telephoto: When it comes to zooming, Google is slightly ahead, offering 5x zoom to Apple's 4x, but in terms of digital zoom, the Pixel 11 Pro's 120x zoom towers over Apple's 40x zoom—in a way. Google's "pro zoom" is built on generative AI, producing plausible details for things it can't see, leading to a realistic-looking photo. Apple's approach uses AI more modestly, focusing on stacking multiple exposures to reduce noise and fill in details. The end result: Apple's extreme zoom is more grainy and noisy, but also more real.

Front camera: The Pixel has a real advantage here with a 42MP sensor compared to Apple's 18MP selfie camera.

Both lines of smart phone cameras are roughly equal in terms of raw power. The main difference is largely a philosophical one. Apple might be losing the extreme magnification fight by capping its digital zoom to a relatively modest 40x, but it's also avoiding producing photos that are largely a product of artificial intelligence. If you want to push the boundaries of what a lens can capture with the help of generative AI, and you're not overly concerned about verisimilitude, the Pixel is the choice. If you want to keep it real (well, real-ish, anyway) the iPhone is the choice.

title: Six New Features Coming to the Pixel Watch 5
description: Google's newest Pixel Watch comes with some exclusive features and changes.
fullText:
At first glance, you might think Google's new Pixel Watch 5 was actually the Pixel Watch 4. That's because it has the same "Actua 360 display" at an identical 320 PPI with up to 3,000 nits of brightness. And, just like the Pixel Watch 4, you can get the Pixel Watch 5 in either 41mm or 45mm models. If not for the new colors, you might think this year's watch is just like last year's watch.

It doesn't help that many of the newest software features that Google announced along with the Pixel Watch 5 are compatible with older watches, too. Things like "Health Guardian," which tracks trends in insulin resistance, blood pressure, and sleep breathing, will be available on Pixel Watch 4 when they launch, just as they will be on Pixel Watch 5. But while the Pixel Watch 5 is a small update to the Pixel Watch 4, it is an update: There are six new features exclusive to the watch that you won't find on older models.

The Pixel Watch 4 runs the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 chip; the Pixel Watch 5 runs the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 Accelerated chip. That might not sound like a big difference, and, indeed, we don't have benchmarks at this time to say just how much faster the Pixel Watch 5 is than its predecessor.

However, according to Google, the Pixel 5's "Accelerated" chip is powering on-device AI features faster than before. That includes Google's "Raise to Talk" feature, which lets you interact with Gemini by raising your wrist. The company says these features on Pixel Watch 5 now process "instantly with low latency," even when you aren't connected to the internet.

The chip also powers Gemini Intelligence Proactive Suggestions (Google previously called this Magic Cue). These are new suggestions that automatically appear based on the context of what you're doing: If someone asks you for your flight info, Gemini can use your Pixel Watch 5's chip to dig through your apps to surface that info by presenting it as an option to share with a tap. Google says the Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 Accelerated chip has 50% more RAM than the previous generation, as well as a 12% CPU boost, which makes the whole chip 20% faster overall.

Google has some bold claims for the Pixel Watch 5. Not only does the company claim that its newest watch has the most accurate GPS route tracking of any Pixel Watch (the company says it has double the accuracy of previous generations in the "toughest environments"), Google says its more accurate than Apple Watch Ultra 3 and Garmin Fenix 8 Pro. We'll have to see how true those claims are when reviewers put the watch to the test.

To make these leaps in GPS route tracking, Google says it tapped into Google Maps to "trace satellite ray paths through 3D building models." The company also explains how Pixel Watch 5 can connect to weather reference stations around the globe in real time to adjust for local atmospheric conditions. Google claims all these steps improve route precision.

While Pixel Watch 4 shares many of the new health features Google is rolling out in coming months, the Pixel Watch 5 does win in certain categories. Google says the newest watch has 15% more accurate sleep stage detection, which should improve sleep tracking overall. In addition, your bedtime automation on the Pixel Watch 5 can pause audiobooks automatically when you fall asleep, and there's now a dedicated bedtime watch face.

Google says Pixel Watch 5 comes with two new "stunning" watch faces, as well as 11 new "glanceable" complication styles. The company didn't highlight what those looked like in their press releases, but 9to5Google has images of the faces (Weave and Chronograph). You can also use AI to generate new watch faces if the available options aren't to your liking.

Google says the Watch 5 has three new color options, though only two are available in both sizes. Those include Fog, Olive, and Canyon, though the latter is a 41mm exclusive. If you're set on the 45mm model, you could instead choose the Stephen Curry Special Edition, as that model isn't available in 41mm.

One health feature exclusive to Pixel Watch 5 is "breathing emergency detection." Google says the Pixel Watch 5 can use on-device AI to read its PPG, accelerometer, and barometer sensors all at once, in an effort to detect if you stop breathing. That could be from drug toxicity accidents, pneumonia, or choking. The company says if your watch detects a breathing emergency and you can't respond, it will reach out to emergency services on your behalf, even sharing your live location. This feature is launching in Europe first.

title: You Can Still Get a Samsung Galaxy Z Phone With a $350 Amazon Gift Card
description: The Galaxy Z Flip8, Galaxy Z Fold8, and Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra phones are all up for grabs with Amazon gift cards and trade-in credits.
fullText:
Samsung announced five new products during its Galaxy Unpacked event last month. Three of those are the new flagship smartphones: the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra, and Z Flip 8. Amazon had pre-order deals that were supposed to last until their launch, but the deal is still active after their release. We don't know for how long, so if you're interested, get it before it's gone. You can get an Amazon gift card up to $350, while Samsung is offering a max of $230 in Samsung credits. And if you're looking to switch to T-Mobile, you can get a Galaxy Z Fold 8 on them. You can read more details on that deal here.

If you were expecting a shiny new toy from the Z Flip 8, you might be disappointed—it's not that different from the Z Flip 7. It has a 4.1-inch outer display and a 6.9-inch inner display, 12GB of RAM, and similar cameras to the Z Flip 7, including a 50MP Wide, 12MP Ultra Wide, and 10X Digital Zoom. As Lifehacker Senior Tech Editor Jake Peterson says, the Z Fold 8 is not the upgraded version of the Z Fold 7: It's a brand new device, which might appeal to users who want a phablet that takes up a little less space in their pocket.
